## 2. Disposition notation

- `R(op)`: throwing business read. The top-level owner pre-creates/adopts one
  trace; failure is captured and preserves the last loaded projection. Only a
  table-declared true not-found may become absence.
- `W(op)`: throwing business write. Failure captures the same trace and stops
  dependent actions, local success state, and success toast; transaction
  rollback is preserved.
- `KR(account)`: Keychain get. Only `errSecItemNotFound` is absent; every other
  OSStatus is a typed read failure.
- `KW(op)`: Keychain set/delete. Failure is captured and never reports saved,
  removed, connected, or authorized success.
- `D(op, policy)`: ContextDependencyLoader. Required blocks the Card as
  `context_unavailable`; optionalApproved commits failure+degradation before a
  visible missing marker and continuation.
- `P!(op)`: explicit throwing decode; mutation paths decode before first write
  or roll back completely.
- `PI(op)`: explicit invalid projection carrying the trace; never absence.
- `C(op)`: the only residual form, an annotated cancellation-only sleep.

Internal table-case contracts used below (ordinary single `@Test` owners; no
Swift Testing `@Test(arguments:)`):

- `R[x]`: `businessReadFailureProducesFailedTraceAndPreservesPriorValue(x)`
- `W[x]`: `businessWriteFailureProducesFailedTraceAndDoesNotAdvance(x)`
- `KR[x]`: `keychainReadDistinguishesNotFoundFromFailure(x)`
- `KW[x]`: `keychainMutationFailureNeverReportsSuccess(x)`
- `D[x,p]`: `dependencyFailureHonorsRequiredVsOptionalApproved(x,p)`
- `P[x]`: `invalidPayloadIsTraceableAndNeverDefaults(x)`
- `C[x]`: `cancellationSleepIsExpectedAndStateSafe(x)`

Every R/W/K/D regression asserts UI trace equals `failure_record.id`, or the
same logger trace when the DB itself is unavailable. Every mutation parse test
also asserts zero partial writes.

## 6.1 Literal descriptor → production seam registry

This registry is relational, not prose. Its `Tags` cell grammar is one or more
comma-separated backticked literal tags. The gate mechanically expands every
cell, requires each of the 133 §3–§6 tags exactly once, and joins by unique tag
to recover its entry pathname. Exactly 131 are production descriptors; the
final two are TestSuite-helper descriptors and deliberately have no production
seam/delegate/counter. `none` means Core-only. Delegate edges use exact
backticked `path::containing declaration`; when the direct App call enters a
seam other than the descriptor's primary seam, the tuple is followed by the
exact literal `=> <seam-case>`. Otherwise the tuple's seam is the primary seam.
Two or more tuples in one cell are separated only by literal `<br>`, never
slash/“and” shorthand. The scanner requires one matching
`P1-B-DELEGATE <stable-edge-id> <seam>` at every listed edge. Owner aliases are
closed and expand only as follows; a suite name is never an owner alias:

|---|---|

| `A2` | `ApplicationWorkflowTests.workflowProjectionPreservesPriorValueOnRefreshFailure` |

### 8.5 Catch descriptor → production seam registry

This registry mechanically expands every backticked `E[...]` tag and requires
the exact 134-row §8.1–§8.4 set once, with no duplicate or orphan. `none` is a
Core-only edge. Every non-`none` edge is the exact pathname and containing
declaration/call anchor of one
`P1-B-DELEGATE <stable-edge-id> <seam>` marker. `A13` is the
descriptor table inside
`ApplicationWorkflowTests.committedVisibilityFailureCannotRepeatMutation`;
the named direct tests remain additional semantic evidence, not substitute
set-membership checks. The only owner aliases are the fully qualified entries
in §6.1. Existing GuideChat/Schedule declarations may add supplemental
semantic evidence, but a suite name is never an alias or a second primary
owner. In §8.5 and the planned-catch table only, an owner cell written
`<primary> / <supplemental>...` is an ordered closed syntax: the leftmost alias
is the descriptor's one primary owner and every later alias is supplemental
evidence. Supplemental aliases never satisfy owner-set membership or add a
second descriptor owner.

(36 calls plus one helper declaration), and two additional

allowance. Final count for every named raw formatter is zero.

| Entry site | Current bypass | Candidate 03 terminal |

Two additional force-try sites are not silent fallbacks: `AppStore.swift:573`
database initialization becomes the fixed safe pre-composition fail-fast
boundary above; `AppStore.swift:690` Coding Ranch bootstrap becomes a captured
visible failure on the real DB and keeps dispatch halted. Final AppStore
`try!` count is zero.

##### 4. Canonical occurrence and group encoding

Entry and final identities are deliberately distinct. Each entry occurrence is
serialized as UTF-8 fields joined by one NUL byte:

```text
CandidateOccurrenceV1 =
  exactPath NUL
  DeclarationID NUL
  SyntaxClass.rawValue NUL
  CandidateNodeTokens NUL
  Left16SignificantTokens NUL
  Right16SignificantTokens NUL
  sameWindowOrdinalDecimal

entryAnchorDigest = lowercaseHex(SHA256(CandidateOccurrenceV1))
EntryOccurrenceID = "EF-E-" + entryAnchorDigest
```

`sameWindowOrdinal` is one-based within `(path, DeclarationID, SyntaxClass,
CandidateNodeTokens, Left16, Right16)` in source byte order. It makes identical
repeated expressions distinct without using a line number.

`DeclarationID` is canonical innermost type plus declaration base name and
external parameter labels, for example
`AppStore.nextScheduleMenuTitle(now:)`,
`PlanningEntryCoordinator.prepareManual(snapshot:pending:forceNewCommand:)`,
or `ScheduleManagerView.body`. A top-level callable uses the literal owner
`<file>`. Access modifiers, generic names, parameter/return types,
line numbers, and whitespace are not part of the identity. Closure-initialized
locals are never treated as computed properties. An occurrence that
cannot be assigned to exactly one function/init/subscript/computed property is
an unclassified scanner error.

`CandidateNodeTokens` is the normalized scanner trigger span, not a claimed
Swift AST expression: an operator/keyword/call trigger, guard through its
specific exit token, explicit-discard marker, or explicit registered aggregate
anchor. The adjacent sixteen significant tokens on each side provide the
line-independent local anchor. Tokens preserve identifier/literal spelling,
normalize whitespace, and omit comments/ordinary string bodies; exact SQL
aggregate anchors are explicit registry entries because their text is masked.

Final source is scanned with the same anchor serialization and the ID prefix is
`EF-F-`; the `EF-E`/`EF-F` prefix, not a different hashed version literal,
distinguishes stage. A token-identical retained anchor therefore has the same
64-hex suffix. The terminal relation uses only the normative §6 source grammar:
`KEEP`, `DELETE`, or `PLANNED`. `retained` versus `rewritten` is derived from a
KEEP suffix comparison, never written as an implementer-selected action.

The relation is evidence, never implementation authority. It cannot change a
ClassificationSet, disposition, terminal, callable, seam, delegate, owner, or
counter chosen elsewhere in the frozen plan. Cross-gate references are members
of `ClassificationSet`, not a fourth action. Every business entry ID appears
exactly once as a KEEP or DELETE source; harmless resolution is automatic. Every
scanned final candidate ID appears exactly once as KEEP, exact harmless retain,
or PLANNED. DELETE has no final candidate ID but still requires every descriptor/
cross reference's frozen closure. A final candidate with no relation is unknown
and fails.

Rows are compressed only after occurrence IDs exist:

```text
OccurrenceGroupV1 =
  "OccurrenceGroupV1" NUL exactPath NUL DeclarationID NUL SyntaxClass NUL ClassificationSet NUL
  sorted(EntryOccurrenceID).joined(NUL)

groupDigest = lowercaseHex(SHA256(OccurrenceGroupV1))
```

`ClassificationSet` is either one harmless reason or a sorted, unique `+`
joined set of one or more descriptor/cross references:

```text
descriptor:<tag>:<typed|capture|approved-residual>
cross:<literal|catch|raw>:<tag>
harmless:<HarmlessReason.rawValue>
```

A harmless classification may never be combined with another reference.
Multiple references are required where one lexical occurrence joins more than
one independently frozen tag; silently choosing only one is a ledger error.

The review document may store one row per group rather than 954 prose rows,
but every row MUST store path, DeclarationID, syntax class, ClassificationSet,
count, sorted full EntryOccurrenceIDs, and groupDigest. A digest without the sorted
EntryOccurrenceIDs is not independently reviewable and is forbidden in the final
freeze.

##### 5. Scanner grammar

1. `entry-current` verifies the exact path set and entry hashes before scanning;
   `final` instead extracts and validates the five frozen ledger streams
   §9.1b–§9.1f, all three framed Python sources §9.1g, §9.1g-p, and §9.1g-v,
   and the §9.1h compiler-typed role registry, then scans the exact 43 terminal
   paths.
2. Run a length-preserving Swift lexical projection. Preserve newlines and
   byte offsets. Mask `//` comments, recursively nested `/* ... */` comments,
   and normal/raw/single-line/multiline string bodies. Recursively scan only
   Swift interpolation expressions whose backslash has the exact raw-string
   hash count; raw hash count is unbounded. A physical newline in a nontriple
   string, or any unterminated comment/string/interpolation, is fatal.
3. Tokenize Swift identifiers, literals, delimiters, and maximal-munch
   operators. Comments and ordinary string contents never create candidates;
   interpolation code does. This is required for the schedule budget
   coalescing expression embedded in a string.
4. Emit all 200 entry `??` tokens. Entry mode emits each whitespace-delimited
   lone ternary `?`; final mode also recognizes `a?b:c` by a same-delimiter-
   depth colon, so removing spaces cannot evade the gate. Exactly 486 entry
   lone questions are frozen as `SX-E` exclusions by the same declaration +
   trigger + 16-token-window + ordinal identity. Final mode first joins that
   exact ID set; a changed/new lone question is excluded only by §5.2's closed
   delimiter-aware Optional-type-postfix grammar. Changed/new Optional chaining,
   `as?`, optional patterns, and every other lone `?` are candidates or fatal
   ambiguities. Emit every `default:` owned by a switch.
5. Emit each `return`, `continue`, or `break` owned by a `guard ... else`
   body as one `guardEarlyExit`; one guard with two exit tokens is two
   occurrences.
6. Scan every `.compactMap`, `.filter`, `.map`, and `.flatMap` call first.
   Exact entry classifications partition them: 16 compactMap plus 35 collection
   filters are drop candidates; 23 proven Optional/Result projections are
   candidates; 60 query filters and 54 collection maps are exact `SX-E`
   exclusions. Every one of the 114 entry exclusion IDs is stored in the
   expanded registry. Final mode preserves an exact exclusion suffix, admits a
   changed/new filter only through §5.2's closed GRDB receiver/shape/terminal
   grammar, and rejects a changed/new collection map/flatMap. A proven
   Optional/Result projection remains a candidate; unresolved receiver identity
   is fatal, never assumed collection/query or harmless.
7. Scan every explicit `_ =` and every call-headed expression statement owned
   by a brace scope before making any semantic claim. The syntax-only universe
   is exactly 2,283: 17 explicit discards plus 2,266 standalone call roots.
   Exact EF-E identity joins select the reviewed 80
   `ignoredNonVoidResult` candidates (17 explicit discards plus 63
   bare/membership/yield sites); the remaining 2,203 roots are frozen as
   `unreviewedStandaloneCallSyntax` entry exclusions. The lexical scanner never
   infers a return type, but exact suffix equality alone is not terminal proof:
   §5.3's compiler-typed evidence must independently close every retained
   standalone root. SwiftUI/result-builder roots and framework/external calls
   stay expanded entry syntax exclusions, not claimed `Void` calls. Binding, assignment,
   `return`, `throw`, control conditions, nested arguments, and top-level
   binary/ternary sequences are not statement roots. Final source must join
   each root to one of the exact 80 candidate IDs or exact 2,203 exclusion IDs,
   and every retained exclusion must also pass the frozen typed role; unknown
   or unresolved syntax/type is fatal. The eight planned-new paths expect zero bare roots
   and zero explicit discards; side-effect-only Void work uses an explicit
   typed binding such as `let _: Void = ...`.
8. Emit every `try!` and every lexical catch arm. Literal `try?`, raw
   formatter, and catch semantic gates retain their independent scanners and
   are joined by occurrence/tag rather than recounted.
9. Emit every direct Swift/process terminal in the closed name set
   `fatalError|preconditionFailure|precondition|assertionFailure|assert|abort|exit|_exit`.
   Entry count is exactly nine: Planning resolver one, Orchestrator five, and
   AppStore three. The six Core invariant traps are
   `harmless:closedExplicitTrap`. Preview-default construction is not closed:
   it joins `N[.applicationPrecompositionFailFast]` and must move behind the
   same pre-composition boundary as the database-open `try!`; the state-directory
   and runtime-bootstrap AppStore fatals cross their exact E catch descriptors.
10. Emit every nonthrowing Result wrapper in the exact syntax family
    `Result(catching:)` or `Result { try ... }` as
    `nonthrowingResultWrapper`. Entry count is zero. Final source permits only
    `ApplicationPostDatabaseBootstrapBoundary.ensureCodingRanchBootstrap(trace:_:)`
    joining `N[.codingRanchBootstrapCapture]:capture`; any other wrapper is
    unknown and fails.
11. Emit all `max`, `min`, `.clamped`, and `addingReportingOverflow` calls in
   the 43-path set (8 max + 2 min + 0 clamped + 4 overflow). Additionally emit
   exactly the three persistent/business arithmetic anchors: Run attempt
   increment, SQL spend aggregate, and planning-token reduce. New arithmetic
   in the closed budget/spend/token/attempt owner declarations is fatal;
   display index math, loop-dominated bounds, String/Array concatenation, and
   Double geometry are exact exclusions, not heuristic omissions.
12. Assign exactly one containing DeclarationID and one occurrence ID. Sort by
    raw UTF-8 path, declaration, class, then source byte offset only for
    generation; byte offset is never persisted as identity.

###### 5.1 Frozen syntax-exclusion registry

An exclusion is not a candidate classification and cannot be created by the
implementer. Each entry is serialized with the same path, canonical
DeclarationID, normalized trigger, left/right sixteen-token windows, and
same-window ordinal used for candidates, substituting `ExclusionKind` for
`SyntaxClass`. A core entry exclusion uses `SX-E-` plus the lowercase SHA-256
suffix and its terminal identity uses `SX-F-`. A standalone-call entry
exclusion uses `SC-X-` plus its independently frozen lowercase SHA-256 suffix
and its terminal identity uses `SC-F-`. Neither prefix family may be substituted
for the other.

```text
frozenLoneQuestion       486
frozenOptionalChainingDot 159
collectionMapOrFlatMap    54
queryFilter               60
unreviewedStandaloneCallSyntax 2203
TOTAL                   2962
coreRegistryDigest ab533c5721819c7a8af22515247e85ae8b5af8d3de1b0d4e2f30a6c3f01ed5c5
standaloneRegistryDigest 998a30e237cbf6f127fcbc6db8e6887e9c5a0be57a27809727a680bc3ef346d1
unionRegistryDigest 808dd09fc37cf71ce6fa83a872741caf40ae6c2b4ccb904f56d3630e992758dc
```

The core digest serialization is
`"SyntaxExclusionRegistryV1" NUL sorted(full SX-E IDs).joined(NUL)`.
The standalone digest serialization is
`"StandaloneCallSyntaxExclusionRegistryV1" NUL sorted(full SC-X IDs).joined(NUL)`;
the union digest serialization is
`"P1BExpandedSyntaxExclusionUnionV1" NUL sorted(all SX-E and SC-X IDs).joined(NUL)`.
The expanded 2,962-row ID/path/DeclarationID/kind set in inline §9.1f is
mandatory freeze data, not optional evidence. It contains all 759 core syntax
exclusions and all 2,203 standalone-call exclusions in one canonical stream.

##### 5.2 Entry exclusions and final structural exclusions

The 2,962 §9.1f exclusions are exact **entry** evidence, not an exact
final-count allowlist. Final exclusions use the `SX-F-`/`SC-F-` prefix with the
same serialization and digest suffix. An entry exclusion is retained only by
an identical final suffix; otherwise it is deleted. Thus
`|Xretained| + |Xdeleted| = 2,962`; final exclusion cardinality is intentionally
not frozen because planned DTOs and deleted source change legal syntax.

A changed or new final token is excluded without an entry identity only by the
following closed structural rules. These rules produce an exclusion, never a
harmless CandidateOccurrence classification:

1. A changed/new lone `?` is structurally excluded only when the delimiter-
   aware parser proves an Optional **type postfix** in a type declaration,
   annotation, generic argument, cast target, or function result. Exact `try?`
   is owned by the independent 133-row literal gate and is excluded from
   ternary parsing only after that lexical owner is proven. Optional chaining
   (`?.`, `?[`, or `?(`), `as?`, and optional-pattern matching may remain
   excluded only by an exact frozen §9.1f suffix; a changed/new occurrence is a
   candidate/fatal ambiguity, never a dynamic structural exclusion. Every
   other lone `?`, including whitespace-free `a?b:c`, is a ternary candidate.
2. A changed or new `.filter` is a GRDB query exclusion only when its direct
   named receiver belongs to the closed receiver set mechanically extracted
   from §9.1f's 60 entry `queryFilter` rows, or the receiver is declared in one
   of the eight planned-new paths by a same-file `struct` that explicitly lists
   `FetchableRecord` and `PersistableRecord`/`TableRecord`. The same chained
   expression must use `.filter(Column(...))` and terminate in the closed set
   `fetchOne|fetchAll|fetchCursor|fetchCount|deleteAll|updateAll` (allowing only
   `order|limit|select` between filter and terminal). Closure-form `.filter {}`,
   a value/collection receiver, unresolved receiver, split request stored for
   later, or unknown intermediate/terminal is not a query exclusion.
3. A collection `.map`/`.flatMap` exclusion and every standalone-call exclusion
   must retain an exact frozen entry suffix **and** pass §5.3's current typed-
   AST proof. No changed/new or suffix-identical receiver/callee is inferred to
   be Collection/Void from lexical bytes. A new or renamed collection map/
   flatMap or call-headed expression statement is fatal. Planned side-effect-only work must use an
   explicit typed binding such as `let _: Void = call()` or `return call()`; it
   may not create a bare root. `let _: Void =` is not the scanner's explicit-
   discard `_ =` form.
4. Optional/Result projections remain candidates when the receiver is proven
   Optional/Result; an unresolved projection receiver is fatal. All other
   candidate classes have no dynamic harmless/exclusion escape.

##### 5.3 Compiler-typed closure of retained call/map/query exclusions

The 2,203 standalone-call, 54 collection-map, and 60 GRDB-query entry rows are
freeze-time lexical identities, not self-proving return/type classifications.
A retained suffix is accepted only after the same source range joins a complete
typed-AST evidence row generated from the authoritative SwiftPM target job in
both debug and release. The toolchain full version, SDK/target, semantic driver
arguments, exact source set, and deterministic argument transform are frozen
with the scanner. For each target/configuration it derives the existing
SwiftPM frontend job, removes only object/module/dependency/index/cache output
arguments, routes every cache to a fresh outside-workspace directory, and runs
one `swiftc -frontend ... -typecheck -dump-ast -dump-ast-format json
-primary-file <path>` job per final production path while retaining all other
target sources as context. Whole-module concatenated JSON is forbidden. A
nonzero exit, diagnostic, malformed/non-dict JSON, compiler/schema/version
drift, missing active branch, or zero/multiple canonical source nodes is fatal.
Debug and release evidence for a root active in both must agree; every retained
row must appear in at least one real configuration, so a both-inactive `#if`
cannot hide it.

Canonical AST matching uses the final lexical statement/root byte range plus
source filename. It ignores compiler-cloned `processed_init` subtrees and
deduplicates only nodes with identical source range, kind, selected
`decl_usr`/`type_usr`, static type, and ancestor role. It freezes the selected
callee/module/USR, static expression type, and the exact closed consumption
role. A standalone exclusion is legal only as one of:

- exact static `Void` (`$sytD`);
- `consumedImplicitReturn`/explicit return, proved by the compiler's exact
  return node and a matching enclosing result type;
- `consumedByExactFrozenBuilder`, proved by the compiler-inserted
  `buildExpression`/builder chain for a frozen external builder USR; a file,
  `View` return type, custom/new builder, or enclosing closure alone is never
  proof;
- `crossClassConsumed`, when the identical canonical source root is already
  consumed exactly once by a frozen EF/PF candidate such as the closed
  `explicitTrapCall`; Never is legal only through that control-flow candidate;
- `optionalVoidEvaluation`, when the retained `?.` row and innermost selected
  call prove `Void` before optional lifting;
- a frozen external `@discardableResult` or narrow DSL privilege whose exact
  module, callee USR, static result type, and enclosing compiler role appear in
  the reviewed typed-role registry. Author-controlled local
  `@discardableResult`, local return-type changes, new builder overloads, and
  name-only GRDB/Task/framework matches cannot create a privilege.

The GRDB schema-DSL privilege is limited to exact reviewed GRDB callee USRs and
their exact migration/create/alter closure ancestry. `Task` construction is a
separate exact external-USR privilege and never treated as Void. All ordinary
non-Void/unresolved roots are candidates or fatal, including a callee whose
return changes while its lexical call site remains identical.

Each retained collection-map row must select the frozen Swift standard-library
`Sequence`/`Collection.map` (or the separately frozen exact standard-library
variant) USR, with a receiver statically conforming to the frozen protocol and
not Optional, Result, or custom. Each retained query-filter row must resolve a
type-expression receiver and the exact frozen GRDB filter/intermediate/terminal
USR chain; a same-spelled local/parameter/property receiver is fatal. The gate
freezes the exact number of lexical-to-AST joins and requires zero unjoined,
ambiguous, or newly privileged rows. Compiler success alone is not evidence
that this traversal ran.

The final lexer retains the frozen comment/string/raw-string/multiline masking
and exact-hash interpolation recursion. It scans every candidate universe
first, applies exact retained entry exclusions, and only then applies the
closed structural rules above. Deleted entry exclusions require no marker.
Any token left in neither the candidate set nor those exclusions is fatal; any
candidate left outside the BK/HR/PLANNED union is fatal.

##### 6. Terminal occurrence resolution (normative)

The 35 entry hashes and eight `ABSENT` states are **freeze-time evidence only**.
Before Candidate03 Revision03 is frozen, the entry-mode reference scan MUST
reproduce the inline annexes and their reviewed hashes. After implementation
those entry bytes no longer exist; terminal tests MUST NOT rescan current
production files as "entry", require the 35 old hashes to match, or reconstruct
old bytes. Terminal authority is the frozen inline §9.1b–§9.1f ledger data,
all three framed Python sources in §9.1g, §9.1g-p, and §9.1g-v, the §9.1h
compiler-typed role registry, and the closed seventeen-row planned tuple registry. Test 18's internal terminal-gate
subcase parses those frozen annexes and independently scans the 43 final
production paths.

Let `E` be the 954 entry IDs parsed from §9.1b. Partition it from its frozen
`ClassificationSet`, never from final source:

```text
B = { e in E | classification(e) is descriptor/cross }  // 431
H = { e in E | classification(e) is harmless }          // 523
```

`B` contains 386 groups and 492 occurrence-weighted semantic references: 244
`descriptor:` plus the exact 248 `cross:` tuples. `H` contains 386 groups. The
772 groups expand to 954 distinct IDs.

Final source uses exactly this grammar; IDs are lowercase 64-hex:

```swift
// P1-B-RESOLVE KEEP EF-E-<64hex> EF-F-<64hex>
// P1-B-RESOLVE DELETE EF-E-<64hex> NONE
// P1-B-RESOLVE PLANNED PF-P-<64hex> EF-F-<64hex>
```

`P1-B-RESOLVE` is the sole entry-to-final occurrence relation. The following
non-catch tag/disposition markers remain semantic markers and omit occurrence
IDs:

```swift
// P1-B-EQUIVALENT <typed|capture|approved-residual> N[.<tag>]
// P1-B-EQUIVALENT-CROSS <literal|catch|raw> <tag>
```

For expression/statement-owned candidates (`??`, ternary, guard exit,
projection, ignored result, `try!`, trap, numeric, Result wrapper), the
contiguous marker block contains first the semantic lines in exact sorted
ClassificationSet-ref order, then the resolution lines in relation-ID order,
and immediately precedes the candidate-containing executable statement. For a
switch `default:`, the same block immediately precedes that exact `default:`
label. A `nonthrowingSwallowCatch` uses one special contiguous
body block in this exact order: (1) the required `P1-B-CATCH` semantic marker
as the first nonempty lexical body line, (2) its sorted `P1-B-RESOLVE` line(s),
then (3) the first executable statement. `P1-B-CATCH` is the sole disposition/
tag semantic marker for that catch; it replaces, rather than duplicates, a
`P1-B-EQUIVALENT` or `P1-B-EQUIVALENT-CROSS` line. No blank line, attribute,
unrelated comment, declaration, or code may intervene. Resolution lines are
sorted by first ID. `KEEP`/`PLANNED` must name the unique scanner candidate in
the attached statement, label, or enclosing catch arm.

The stated `EF-F` MUST equal the final scanner ID for that exact candidate.
Every final candidate named by KEEP or PLANNED accepts exactly one resolution
line. An exact-suffix harmless retain has no resolution line and is consumed
only by the automatic H rule below. `KEEP` preserves the
frozen `exactPath`, `DeclarationID`, and `ClassificationSet`. A KEEP may change
the scanner syntax class/node/windows/ordinal only inside that same declaration
when the frozen semantic contract requires a real rewrite. Identical EF-E/EF-F
digest suffixes are mechanically reported as `retained`; different suffixes are
reported as `rewritten`. This label is derived, not chosen by the implementer.
Moving an occurrence across a pathname or DeclarationID is never KEEP: the old
entry must close through DELETE, while a genuinely planned new occurrence must
match an exact PF-P tuple. If several old IDs with the same frozen
ClassificationSet and exact production owner could name one consolidated final
candidate, the lexicographically smallest eligible EF-E ID is `KEEP` and every
other eligible old ID is `DELETE`.

`DELETE` is never inferred from a missing marker for `B`. The scanner expands
the 131 production literal tags, 134 E tags, and 130 existing-N tags into the
exact 395-tag descriptor registry, then reads the entry ClassificationSet in
its already frozen exact-sorted reference order and maps every
`descriptor:`/`cross:` ref to its frozen primary seam. The
`DeletionOwnerSeam` is the primary seam of that exact-sorted set's first
reference. This first-reference rule selects only the static source host; it
does not change any descriptor primary, terminal, owner, delegate, variant, or
counter obligation belonging to any other reference in the set. Every one of
the 431 B occurrences is DELETE-eligible under that deterministic host rule.
Its static owner block uses this exact contiguous order immediately before the
selected seam callable declaration:

```swift
// P1-B-SEAM <DeletionOwnerSeam>
// P1-B-EQUIVALENT... / P1-B-EQUIVALENT-CROSS...  // exact sorted refs
// P1-B-RESOLVE DELETE EF-E-<64hex> NONE           // sorted IDs
<callable declaration>
```

No blank line, attribute, unrelated comment, or declaration may split the
block. Several DELETE IDs may share a callable block; each keeps its own frozen
ClassificationSet, and the semantic-line union must equal the sorted union of
all those sets with no missing/extra ref. App delegate edges and executed
owners remain independently mandatory but never select or host the DELETE.
Static owner placement alone is insufficient: the descriptor-variant gate must
invoke this exact seam callable and assert its frozen counter, original trace,
terminal, persistence/log/UI evidence, and primary owner. Thus a comment-only
tombstone, a marker in a different declaration, a generic reporter/helper, or
an unexecuted seam fails. Every reference MUST still join its exact descriptor/
gate tag, callable, seam, delegate (where any), owner, and expected counter
case. The deleted EF-E digest suffix MUST be absent from the final candidate
set, and the EF-E ID may occur on no other resolution line.

For the 379 groups / 423 occurrences whose references all project to one
primary seam, the rule naturally selects that seam. For the seven groups /
eight occurrences whose references project to multiple seams, it selects the
first exact-sorted reference's seam while the descriptor-variant gate still
executes and proves every reference's independent callable/delegate/owner/
counter closure. No B occurrence is forced to retain syntax merely because its
ClassificationSet spans seams; the 431/523/17/448 arithmetic is unchanged.

Every `b in B` has exactly one KEEP or DELETE line. Missing, duplicate, and
unknown EF-E IDs fail. Consequently deletion cannot consume an unknown final
candidate: after relations are joined, every final candidate still MUST be
consumed exactly once by one B/KEEP, one H exact-retain, or one PLANNED row.

Harmless closure is automatic and has no source marker. A final candidate
retains `h in H` only when path, DeclarationID, SyntaxClass, normalized node,
both sixteen-token windows, ordinal, and therefore the 64-hex EF digest suffix
are identical. Absence is an automatic harmless deletion. `H` permits no
rewritten relation and no new harmless reason: an altered or recreated harmless-
looking candidate has a new final ID and is unknown/fatal.

The closed seventeen-row table defines `PlannedOccurrenceV1` as UTF-8 NUL-joined
fields:

```text
"P1BPlannedOccurrenceV1", exactPath, DeclarationID, SyntaxClass,
ExactNormalizedTrigger, ClassificationSet, "1"
```

`PlannedOccurrenceID = "PF-P-" + lowercaseHex(SHA256(PlannedOccurrenceV1))`.
Each tuple has count one. The table is exactly fourteen planned catches plus two
final-only traps plus one final-only Result wrapper. A PLANNED marker must join
the exact tuple and its final candidate; no path/declaration/class/trigger/
classification substitution is allowed. Planned tuples take precedence over
B/KEEP matching.

Define `BK`, `BD`, `HR`, and `HD` as business keep/delete and harmless retained/
deleted sets. The terminal arithmetic is variable only where implementation
legitimately deletes syntax:

```text
BK ∩ BD = ∅; BK ∪ BD = B; |BK| + |BD| = 431
HR ∩ HD = ∅; HR ∪ HD = H; |HR| + |HD| = 523
    |PLANNED| = 17
FinalCandidateSet = final(BK) ⊎ final(HR) ⊎ final(PLANNED)
|FinalCandidateSet| = |BK| + |HR| + 17
    P1-B-RESOLVE line count = 431 + 17 = 448
```

The gate rejects a final candidate with no relation; a relation with no
candidate/terminal; duplicate final IDs; a KEEP whose classification/semantic
marker differs; a DELETE whose semantic refs are not closed; a planned tuple
not realized exactly once; and any attempt to classify a new final candidate
as harmless.

The planning-time gate requires:

```text
scanner(entry bytes).OccurrenceID set == classified ledger ID set
classified IDs are pairwise disjoint
descriptor/cross IDs == 431
closed-nonfallback IDs == 523
union IDs == 954
entry SyntaxExclusionID set == expanded 2,962-ID exclusion union
  (486 lone question + 159 optional-chaining dot +
  54 collection map/flatMap + 60 query filter +
  2,203 standalone-call syntax)
per-class and per-path vectors equal sections 1 and 3
N registry == 130 unique rows with 89/14/27 disposition split
every final candidate in a planned-new path joins one of the exact eight

  Runtime source-stage catches in existing `PlanningProviderResolver.swift`,
  two credential catches in existing `OpenAIOAuthSession.swift`, and one MCP

```

#### §9.1g Inline normative reference scanner source

This complete scanner source is normative and has no generator-path or runtime `/tmp` dependency. The following **freeze-only** bootstrap is independent of all three framed sources. Set `P1B_EXTRACT_DIR` to a fresh existing canonical absolute direct directory outside the repository and run the block from the repository root. Its single inline Python parent opens `/` and traverses every repository and extraction-root component with required `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC` flags, retains both anchor FDs across every child, and descriptor-retraverses their identities plus every extracted source and inventory snapshot before and after each child. From one retained inventory snapshot it checks all three source frames' exact byte/physical-line/SHA metadata, compiles their retained text, and exclusively creates the three source files plus §9.1h through held directory FDs with `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`; no destination is followed or overwritten. It then runs only producer/validator isolated self-probes, scanner `entry-current`, and a byte-identical typed-registry replay. The TSV is data and is not compiled. The bootstrap removes `P1B_TERMINAL_AST_CORPUS` from child environments, never consumes a real corpus, and never invokes scanner `--final`.

```sh
set -eu
p1b_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
p1b_inventory="$p1b_root/docs/collaboration/tasks/2026-07-25-personal-ai-ranch-p1/p1-b-error-visibility/try-question-mark-inventory.md"
p1b_extract_dir="${P1B_EXTRACT_DIR:?set P1B_EXTRACT_DIR to a fresh existing canonical absolute direct directory outside the repository}"
python3 - "$p1b_root" "$p1b_inventory" "$p1b_extract_dir" <<'PY'
from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import stat
import subprocess
import sys

repo_path, inventory_path, extract_path = sys.argv[1:]
INVENTORY_RELATIVE = "docs/collaboration/tasks/2026-07-25-personal-ai-ranch-p1/p1-b-error-visibility/try-question-mark-inventory.md"
SOURCE_HEADINGS = {
    "p1b_normative_reference_scanner.py": "#### §9.1g Inline normative reference scanner source",
    "p1b_terminal_ast_producer.py": "#### §9.1g-p Inline normative terminal AST corpus producer source",
    "p1b_terminal_ast_validator.py": "#### §9.1g-v Inline normative terminal AST corpus validator source",
}
SOURCE_SHA256 = {
    "p1b_normative_reference_scanner.py": "eee7865f2c205b5de46304d0bf10b0d86760609b19c4b4d3b26105ae45f4cfd8",
    "p1b_terminal_ast_producer.py": "860ff4a314c3ddd64c7a44e1c715950cf02470b77b1a20520ba4d5531dcddeca",
    "p1b_terminal_ast_validator.py": "a78b8fc6cf7c8a7510beba1fa7501a208898705cf808d74975dd14c8ce8dcba4",
}
TYPED_NAME = "p1b_typed_role_registry.tsv"
TYPED_SHA256 = "a02c9b8792d4afa22b1801a8ab17354d19b38ef3505b887466581512a6f1422c"
TYPED_BYTES = 2236385
TYPED_LINES = 2478

required_flags = {}
for flag_name in ("O_DIRECTORY", "O_NOFOLLOW", "O_CLOEXEC"):
    value = getattr(os, flag_name, None)
    if type(value) is not int or value == 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"required flag unavailable: {flag_name}")
    required_flags[flag_name] = value
if os.open not in os.supports_dir_fd or os.listdir not in os.supports_fd:
    raise SystemExit("required dir-FD operation unavailable")
DIR_FLAGS = os.O_RDONLY | required_flags["O_DIRECTORY"] | required_flags["O_NOFOLLOW"] | required_flags["O_CLOEXEC"]
READ_FLAGS = os.O_RDONLY | required_flags["O_NOFOLLOW"] | required_flags["O_CLOEXEC"]
CREATE_FLAGS = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | required_flags["O_NOFOLLOW"] | required_flags["O_CLOEXEC"]

def absolute_parts(path: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    if not path.startswith("/") or path == "/" or path.endswith("/") or "//" in path:
        raise SystemExit(f"noncanonical absolute directory spelling: {path!r}")
    parts = tuple(path[1:].split("/"))
    if any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in parts):
        raise SystemExit(f"unsafe absolute component: {path!r}")
    return parts

def relative_parts(path: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    if not path or path.startswith("/") or path.endswith("/") or "//" in path or "\\" in path:
        raise SystemExit(f"unsafe relative spelling: {path!r}")
    parts = tuple(path.split("/"))
    if any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in parts):
        raise SystemExit(f"unsafe relative component: {path!r}")
    return parts

def open_absolute_directory(path: str) -> int:
    parts = absolute_parts(path)
    descriptor = os.open("/", DIR_FLAGS)
    try:
        for component in parts:
            next_descriptor = os.open(component, DIR_FLAGS, dir_fd=descriptor)
            os.close(descriptor)
            descriptor = next_descriptor
        if not stat.S_ISDIR(os.fstat(descriptor).st_mode):
            raise SystemExit(f"anchor is not a directory: {path}")
        return descriptor
    except BaseException:
        os.close(descriptor)
        raise

def directory_identity(descriptor: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    info = os.fstat(descriptor)
    if not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
        raise SystemExit("held anchor changed type")
    return info.st_dev, info.st_ino, stat.S_IFMT(info.st_mode)

def file_identity(info: os.stat_result) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    return info.st_dev, info.st_ino, stat.S_IFMT(info.st_mode), info.st_size

def assert_anchor(descriptor: int, path: str, expected: tuple[int, int, int]) -> None:
    if directory_identity(descriptor) != expected:
        raise SystemExit(f"held anchor identity drift: {path}")
    replay = open_absolute_directory(path)
    try:
        if directory_identity(replay) != expected:
            raise SystemExit(f"pathname anchor identity drift: {path}")
    finally:
        os.close(replay)

def snapshot_relative(anchor: int, relative: str) -> tuple[bytes, tuple[int, int, int, int]]:
    parts = relative_parts(relative)
    opened: list[int] = []
    current = anchor
    try:
        for component in parts[:-1]:
            current = os.open(component, DIR_FLAGS, dir_fd=current)
            opened.append(current)
        descriptor = os.open(parts[-1], READ_FLAGS, dir_fd=current)
        opened.append(descriptor)
        before = os.fstat(descriptor)
        if not stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode):
            raise SystemExit(f"not a direct regular file: {relative}")
        chunks: list[bytes] = []
        while True:
            chunk = os.read(descriptor, 1024 * 1024)
            if not chunk:
                break
            chunks.append(chunk)
        after = os.fstat(descriptor)
        raw = b"".join(chunks)
        identity = file_identity(before)
        if file_identity(after) != identity or len(raw) != before.st_size:
            raise SystemExit(f"file changed during retained read: {relative}")
        return raw, identity
    finally:
        for descriptor in reversed(opened):
            os.close(descriptor)

def write_exclusive(anchor: int, name: str, raw: bytes, mode: int) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
    if relative_parts(name) != (name,):
        raise SystemExit(f"destination must be one component: {name}")
    descriptor = os.open(name, CREATE_FLAGS, mode, dir_fd=anchor)
    try:
        view = memoryview(raw)
        written = 0
        while written < len(view):
            count = os.write(descriptor, view[written:])
            if count <= 0:
                raise SystemExit(f"short extraction write: {name}")
            written += count
        os.fsync(descriptor)
        info = os.fstat(descriptor)
        if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_size != len(raw):
            raise SystemExit(f"extracted file identity/size drift: {name}")
        identity = file_identity(info)
    finally:
        os.close(descriptor)
    os.fsync(anchor)
    return identity

def framed_source(document: str, heading: str) -> bytes:
    matches = list(re.finditer(rf"(?m)^{re.escape(heading)}$", document))
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"heading closure failed: {heading}")
    opening = document.index("```tsv\n", matches[0].end()) + len("```tsv\n")
    closing = document.index("\n```", opening)
    meta_line, separator, source = document[opening:closing + 1].partition("\n")
    match = re.fullmatch(r"# meta\tbytes=([0-9]+)\tlines=([0-9]+)\tsha256=([0-9a-f]{64})", meta_line)
    raw = source.encode("utf-8")
    actual = (len(raw), len(source.splitlines()), hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())
    if not separator or match is None or not source.endswith("\n") or source.endswith("\n\n") or actual != (int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2)), match.group(3)):
        raise SystemExit(f"frame metadata drift: {heading}")
    return raw

def fenced_payload(document: str, heading: str) -> bytes:
    matches = list(re.finditer(rf"(?m)^{re.escape(heading)}$", document))
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise SystemExit(f"heading closure failed: {heading}")
    opening = document.index("```tsv\n", matches[0].end()) + len("```tsv\n")
    closing = document.index("\n```", opening)
    return document[opening:closing + 1].encode("utf-8")

def strict_canonical_object(raw: bytes, label: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    def pairs(rows: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict[str, object]:
        result: dict[str, object] = {}
        for key, value in rows:
            if key in result:
                raise SystemExit(f"duplicate JSON key in {label}: {key}")
            result[key] = value
        return result
    def reject_constant(value: str) -> object:
        raise SystemExit(f"nonfinite JSON in {label}: {value}")
    try:
        value = json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=pairs, parse_constant=reject_constant)
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise SystemExit(f"invalid JSON from {label}") from error
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise SystemExit(f"non-object JSON from {label}")
    canonical = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False).encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
    if raw != canonical:
        raise SystemExit(f"noncanonical JSON from {label}")
    return value

repo_parts = absolute_parts(repo_path)
extract_parts = absolute_parts(extract_path)
if repo_parts == extract_parts or repo_parts == extract_parts[:len(repo_parts)] or extract_parts == repo_parts[:len(extract_parts)]:
    raise SystemExit("repository/extraction-root overlap")
if inventory_path != repo_path + "/" + INVENTORY_RELATIVE:
    raise SystemExit("inventory path spelling drift")
repo_fd = open_absolute_directory(repo_path)
extract_fd = open_absolute_directory(extract_path)
try:
    repo_identity = directory_identity(repo_fd)
    extract_identity = directory_identity(extract_fd)
    assert_anchor(repo_fd, repo_path, repo_identity)
    assert_anchor(extract_fd, extract_path, extract_identity)
    if os.listdir(extract_fd):
        raise SystemExit("freeze extraction root is not empty")
    inventory_raw, inventory_identity = snapshot_relative(repo_fd, INVENTORY_RELATIVE)
    document = inventory_raw.decode("utf-8")
    source_raw = {name: framed_source(document, heading) for name, heading in SOURCE_HEADINGS.items()}
    for name, raw in source_raw.items():
        digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        if digest != SOURCE_SHA256[name]:
            raise SystemExit(f"frozen source SHA drift: {name}")
        compile(raw.decode("utf-8"), f"<embedded-{SOURCE_HEADINGS[name]}>", "exec")
    typed_raw = fenced_payload(document, "#### §9.1h Inline compiler-typed role registry")
    if len(typed_raw) != TYPED_BYTES or len(typed_raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines()) != TYPED_LINES or hashlib.sha256(typed_raw).hexdigest() != TYPED_SHA256:
        raise SystemExit("typed-registry frame drift")
    bindings: dict[str, tuple[bytes, tuple[int, int, int, int]]] = {}
    for name, raw in (*source_raw.items(), (TYPED_NAME, typed_raw)):
        wanted_mode = 0o500 if name.endswith(".py") else 0o400
        created_identity = write_exclusive(extract_fd, name, raw, wanted_mode)
        replay_raw, replay_identity = snapshot_relative(extract_fd, name)
        if replay_raw != raw or replay_identity != created_identity:
            raise SystemExit(f"extracted binding drift: {name}")
        bindings[name] = raw, replay_identity

    def check_epoch() -> None:
        assert_anchor(repo_fd, repo_path, repo_identity)
        assert_anchor(extract_fd, extract_path, extract_identity)
        current_inventory, current_inventory_identity = snapshot_relative(repo_fd, INVENTORY_RELATIVE)
        if current_inventory != inventory_raw or current_inventory_identity != inventory_identity:
            raise SystemExit("inventory identity drift during bootstrap")
        for name, (expected_raw, expected_identity) in bindings.items():
            current_raw, current_identity = snapshot_relative(extract_fd, name)
            if current_raw != expected_raw or current_identity != expected_identity:
                raise SystemExit(f"extracted source identity drift: {name}")

    def run_child(name: str, arguments: list[str], label: str, *, canonical_json: bool) -> bytes:
        if "--final" in arguments or "--ast-corpus" in arguments:
            raise SystemExit("freeze bootstrap attempted real-corpus mode")
        check_epoch()
        environment = dict(os.environ)
        environment.pop("P1B_TERMINAL_AST_CORPUS", None)
        process = subprocess.run([sys.executable, extract_path + "/" + name, *arguments], cwd=repo_path, env=environment, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, check=False)
        check_epoch()
        if process.returncode != 0 or process.stderr != b"":
            raise SystemExit(f"freeze child failed: {label}")
        if canonical_json:
            result = strict_canonical_object(process.stdout, label)
            if result.get("status") != "PASS":
                raise SystemExit(f"freeze child did not PASS: {label}")
        return process.stdout

    producer_result = run_child("p1b_terminal_ast_producer.py", ["--self-test"], "producer-self-test", canonical_json=True)
    validator_result = run_child("p1b_terminal_ast_validator.py", ["--self-test"], "validator-self-test", canonical_json=True)
    entry_result = run_child("p1b_normative_reference_scanner.py", ["--root", repo_path, "--inventory", inventory_path, "--entry-current"], "scanner-entry-current", canonical_json=True)
    typed_replay = run_child("p1b_normative_reference_scanner.py", ["--root", repo_path, "--inventory", inventory_path, "--extract-typed-registry"], "typed-registry-replay", canonical_json=False)
    if typed_replay != typed_raw:
        raise SystemExit("typed-registry replay differs from exclusive extraction")
    check_epoch()
    for result in (producer_result, validator_result, entry_result):
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(result)
    print(json.dumps({"mode": "freeze-bootstrap", "sourceCount": 3, "status": "PASS", "typedRegistrySHA256": TYPED_SHA256}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
finally:
    os.close(extract_fd)
    os.close(repo_fd)
PY
```

The freeze bootstrap stops there. During implementation, after all ten build/link gates, the driver extracts and runs only §9.1g-p against a fresh empty output root, producing a producer-PASS corpus whose validation-handoff destination is still absent. The first and only real-corpus final consumer is the one fresh unfiltered authoritative `RunTests`: its sole TestSuite source gate invokes §9.1g scanner `--final`; that scanner alone extracts and invokes §9.1g-v exactly once, requires the validator's canonical exit-zero result, snapshots its newly exclusively published one-shot handoff, and continues typed extraction from retained bytes. Running the validator directly or a standalone scanner `--final` on that corpus before `RunTests` is forbidden because it would consume the one-shot publication; any failed phase poisons that root and is never retried there.

def _terminal_open_directory_from_root(path: Path) -> int:
    """Open an absolute direct directory one O_NOFOLLOW component at a time."""
    if not path.is_absolute() or any(part in {"", ".", ".."} for part in path.parts[1:]):
        raise ValueError((path, "terminal directory anchor spelling"))
    current = os.open("/", _TERMINAL_DIRECTORY_FLAGS)
    try:
        if not stat.S_ISDIR(os.fstat(current).st_mode):
            raise ValueError((path, "filesystem root is not a directory"))
        for component in path.parts[1:]:
            next_descriptor = os.open(
                component, _TERMINAL_DIRECTORY_FLAGS, dir_fd=current,
            )
            os.close(current)
            current = next_descriptor
            if not stat.S_ISDIR(os.fstat(current).st_mode):
                raise ValueError((path, "terminal anchor component is not directory"))
        return current
    except BaseException:
        os.close(current)
        raise

        return RETAINED_FINAL_SOURCES[path]
    return (ROOT / path).read_text()

def exact_path_vector_digest(paths: list[str]) -> str:
    payload = b"P1BExactPathVectorV2\0" + str(len(paths)).encode() + b"\0"
    payload += b"".join(path.encode() + b"\0" for path in paths)
    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()

def sha(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def mask_swift(
    source: str,
    *,
    line_comments: list[tuple[int, int, str]] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Length-preserving mask; interpolation expressions stay visible."""
    out = list(source)
    n = len(source)

    def blank(a: int, b: int) -> None:
        for k in range(a, b):
            if out[k] not in "\r\n":
                out[k] = " "

    def comment(i: int) -> int:
        if source.startswith("//", i):
            j = source.find("\n", i)
            j = n if j < 0 else j
            if line_comments is not None:
                line_comments.append((i, j, source[i + 2:j]))
            blank(i, j)
            return j
        depth, j = 1, i + 2
        while j < n and depth:
            if source.startswith("/*", j):
                depth += 1
                j += 2
            elif source.startswith("*/", j):
                depth -= 1
                j += 2
            else:
                j += 1
        if depth:
            raise ValueError("unterminated block comment")
        blank(i, j)
        return j

    def string(i: int, hashes: int, triple: bool) -> int:
        quote = '"""' if triple else '"'
        j = i + hashes + len(quote)
        blank(i, j)
        close = quote + ("#" * hashes)
        interpolation = "\\" + ("#" * hashes) + "("
        while j < n:
            if source.startswith(close, j):
                blank(j, j + len(close))
                return j + len(close)
            if source.startswith(interpolation, j):
                blank(j, j + len(interpolation) - 1)
                out[j + len(interpolation) - 1] = "("
                j = code(j + len(interpolation), ")")
                continue
            if not triple and source[j] in "\r\n":
                raise ValueError("unescaped newline in single-line string")
            if not triple and hashes == 0 and source[j] == "\\":
                blank(j, min(n, j + 2))
                j += 2
                continue
            if out[j] not in "\r\n":
                out[j] = " "
            j += 1
        raise ValueError("unterminated string")

    def code(i: int, stop: str | None = None) -> int:
        paren_depth = 0
        while i < n:
            if stop and source[i] == stop and paren_depth == 0:
                out[i] = source[i]
                return i + 1
            if source.startswith("//", i) or source.startswith("/*", i):
                i = comment(i)
                continue
            m = re.match(r'(#{0,})("""|")', source[i:])
            if m:
                i = string(i, len(m.group(1)), m.group(2) == '"""')
                continue
            if stop:
                if source[i] == "(":
                    paren_depth += 1
                elif source[i] == ")":
                    paren_depth -= 1
            i += 1
        if stop:
            raise ValueError("unterminated interpolation")
        return i

    code(0)
    return "".join(out)


TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
    r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*|\d+(?:\.\d+)?|"
    r"\?\?|\?\.|->|==|!=|<=|>=|&&|\|\||\.\.\.|\.\.<|"
    r"[{}()\[\].,:;?+\-*/%!<>=&|\\]"
)

DIRECT_TRAP_CALL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:fatalError|preconditionFailure|precondition|assertionFailure|assert|abort|exit|_exit)\s*\("
)
NONTHROWING_RESULT_WRAPPER_RE = re.compile(
    r"\bResult\s*(?:\(\s*catching\s*:|\{\s*try\b)"
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Span:
    start: int
    end: int


@dataclass
class Occurrence:
    path: str
    declaration: str
    syntax_class: str
    start: int
    end: int
    node: str
    left: str = ""
    right: str = ""
    ordinal: int = 0
    digest: str = ""


@dataclass
class SyntaxExclusion:
    path: str
    declaration: str
    kind: str
    node: str
    left: str
    right: str
    start: int
    ordinal: int = 0
    digest: str = ""


def line_starts(source: str) -> list[int]:
    result = [0]
    for m in re.finditer("\n", source):
        result.append(m.end())
    return result


def offset_for_line(starts: list[int], line: int) -> int:
    return starts[line - 1]


def line_of(starts: list[int], offset: int) -> int:
    lo, hi = 0, len(starts)
    while lo + 1 < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if starts[mid] <= offset:
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid
    return lo + 1


def match_brace(masked: str, opening: int) -> int:
    depth = 0
    for i in range(opening, len(masked)):
        if masked[i] == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif masked[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return i
    raise ValueError("unmatched brace")


DECL_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^[ \t]*(?:@[A-Za-z_][^\n]*\n[ \t]*)*"
    r"(?:(?:public|package|private|fileprivate|internal|open|final|static|class|"
    r"nonisolated|override|mutating|nonmutating|required|convenience|lazy)\s+)*"
    r"(?P<kind>func|init|deinit|subscript)\b"
)
TYPE_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^[ \t]*(?:(?:public|package|private|fileprivate|internal|open|final|indirect)\s+)*"
    r"(?P<kind>actor|class|struct|enum|extension|protocol)\s+(?P<name>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9.]*)"
)
PROPERTY_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^[ \t]*(?:(?:public|package|private|fileprivate|internal|static|class|"
    r"nonisolated|lazy)\s+)*(?:var|let)\s+(?P<name>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)[^\n]*\{"
)


def normalize_tokens(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(TOKEN_RE.findall(text))


def canonical_callable_id(masked: str, start: int, opening: int, owner: str) -> str:
    tokens = [m.group(0) for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(masked[start:opening])]
    kind_index = next(
        (index for index, token in enumerate(tokens) if token in ("func", "init", "deinit", "subscript")),
        None,
    )
    if kind_index is None:
        raise ValueError("callable declaration kind not found")
    kind = tokens[kind_index]
    if kind == "deinit":
        return owner + ".deinit"
    if kind == "func":
        if kind_index + 1 >= len(tokens):
            raise ValueError("function base name not found")
        base = tokens[kind_index + 1]
        search_from = kind_index + 2
    else:
        base = kind
        search_from = kind_index + 1

    try:
        left = tokens.index("(", search_from)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise ValueError(f"parameter list not found for {owner}.{base}") from error
    depth = 0
    right = None
    for index in range(left, len(tokens)):
        token = tokens[index]
        if token == "(":
            depth += 1
        elif token == ")":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                right = index
                break
    if right is None:
        raise ValueError(f"parameter list not closed for {owner}.{base}")

    # Split the parameter list at top-level commas, then take the external
    # label before its top-level colon. Attributes are absent from TOKEN_RE;
    # the first identifier or underscore is therefore the external label.
    segments: list[list[str]] = []
    segment: list[str] = []
    pa = br = cu = angle = 0
    for token in tokens[left + 1:right]:
        if token == "(" : pa += 1
        elif token == ")": pa -= 1
        elif token == "[": br += 1
        elif token == "]": br -= 1
        elif token == "{": cu += 1
        elif token == "}": cu -= 1
        elif token == "<": angle += 1
        elif token == ">" and angle: angle -= 1
        if token == "," and pa == br == cu == angle == 0:
            segments.append(segment)
            segment = []
        else:
            segment.append(token)
    if segment:
        segments.append(segment)

    labels: list[str] = []
    for segment in segments:
        pa = br = cu = angle = 0
        colon = None
        for index, token in enumerate(segment):
            if token == "(": pa += 1
            elif token == ")": pa -= 1
            elif token == "[": br += 1
            elif token == "]": br -= 1
            elif token == "{": cu += 1
            elif token == "}": cu -= 1
            elif token == "<": angle += 1
            elif token == ">" and angle: angle -= 1
            elif token == ":" and pa == br == cu == angle == 0:
                colon = index
                break
        if colon is None:
            raise ValueError(f"parameter colon not found for {owner}.{base}: {segment}")
        prefix = segment[:colon]
        label = next(
            (
                token
                for token in prefix
                if token == "_" or re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*", token)
            ),
            None,
        )
        if label is None:
            raise ValueError(f"external label not found for {owner}.{base}: {segment}")
        labels.append(label)
    label_text = "".join(label + ":" for label in labels)
    return f"{owner}.{base}({label_text})"


def declarations(masked: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, str]]:
    types: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
    for m in TYPE_RE.finditer(masked):
        opening = masked.find("{", m.end())
        if opening < 0:
            continue
        end = match_brace(masked, opening)
        types.append((m.start(), end + 1, m.group("name")))

    def owner_name(pos: int) -> str:
        owners = [x for x in types if x[0] <= pos < x[1]]
        return min(owners, key=lambda x: x[1] - x[0])[2] if owners else "<file>"

    result = list(types)
    for m in DECL_RE.finditer(masked):
        # First brace outside the parameter list is the body opening.
        i, paren, bracket = m.end(), 0, 0
        opening = -1
        while i < len(masked):
            c = masked[i]
            if c == "(":
                paren += 1
            elif c == ")":
                paren -= 1
            elif c == "[":
                bracket += 1
            elif c == "]":
                bracket -= 1
            elif c == "{" and paren == 0 and bracket == 0:
                opening = i
                break
            elif c == "\n" and paren == 0 and bracket == 0 and masked[m.start():i].rstrip().endswith("}"):
                break
            i += 1
        if opening < 0:
            continue
        end = match_brace(masked, opening)
        owner = owner_name(m.start())
        canonical_id = canonical_callable_id(masked, m.start(), opening, owner)
        result.append((m.start(), end + 1, canonical_id))

    for m in PROPERTY_RE.finditer(masked):
        opening = masked.rfind("{", m.start(), m.end())
        if opening < 0:
            continue
        # A stored property with observers has an initializer before its outer
        # brace, so the old blanket `=` rejection incorrectly collapsed every
        # observer body into its containing type.  Parse only top-level
        # `willSet`/`didSet` bodies here.  A closure-initialized stored property
        # (`let x = call { ... }`) has no such accessor and remains excluded.
        has_initializer = "=" in masked[m.start():opening]
        callable_owners = [
            item for item in result[len(types):] if item[0] <= m.start() < item[1]
        ]
        if callable_owners:
            continue
        try:
            end = match_brace(masked, opening)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        owner = owner_name(m.start()) + "." + m.group("name")
        observer_rows: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
        cursor = opening + 1
        depth = 0
        while cursor < end:
            if masked[cursor] == "{":
                depth += 1
                cursor += 1
                continue
            if masked[cursor] == "}":
                if depth:
                    depth -= 1
                cursor += 1
                continue
            if depth == 0:
                accessor = re.match(r"(?:willSet|didSet)\b", masked[cursor:])
                if accessor is not None:
                    kind = accessor.group(0)
                    body_open = cursor + accessor.end()
                    while body_open < end and masked[body_open].isspace():
                        body_open += 1
                    if body_open < end and masked[body_open] == "(":
                        paren = 1
                        body_open += 1
                        while body_open < end and paren:
                            if masked[body_open] == "(":
                                paren += 1
                            elif masked[body_open] == ")":
                                paren -= 1
                            body_open += 1
                        while body_open < end and masked[body_open].isspace():
                            body_open += 1
                    if body_open >= end or masked[body_open] != "{":
                        raise ValueError((owner, kind, "property observer body missing"))
                    body_end = match_brace(masked, body_open)
                    observer_rows.append((cursor, body_end + 1, owner + "." + kind))
                    cursor = body_end + 1
                    continue
            cursor += 1
        if has_initializer:
            if observer_rows:
                result.extend(observer_rows)
            continue
        result.append((m.start(), end + 1, owner))
        result.extend(observer_rows)
    return result


def declaration_for(decls: list[tuple[int, int, str]], pos: int) -> str:
    owners = [x for x in decls if x[0] <= pos < x[1]]
    if not owners:
        return "<file>"
    return min(owners, key=lambda x: x[1] - x[0])[2]


def guard_exits(masked: str) -> list[Span]:
    result: list[Span] = []
    for gm in re.finditer(r"\bguard\b", masked):
        i, pa, br, cu, else_pos = gm.end(), 0, 0, 0, -1
        while i < len(masked):
            c = masked[i]
            if c == "(": pa += 1
            elif c == ")": pa -= 1
            elif c == "[": br += 1
            elif c == "]": br -= 1
            elif c == "{": cu += 1
            elif c == "}":
                if cu: cu -= 1
                else: break
            if pa == br == cu == 0 and re.match(r"else\b", masked[i:]):
                else_pos = i
                break
            i += 1
        if else_pos < 0:
            continue
        opening = masked.find("{", else_pos + 4)
        if opening < 0:
            continue
        closing = match_brace(masked, opening)
        for exit_match in re.finditer(r"\b(?:return|continue|break)\b", masked[opening + 1:closing]):
            pos = opening + 1 + exit_match.start()
            result.append(Span(gm.start(), pos + len(exit_match.group(0))))
    return result


def token_depths(masked: str) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, int, int]], list[tuple[int, int, int]]]:
    toks = [(m.group(0), m.start(), m.end()) for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(masked)]
    depths: list[tuple[int, int, int]] = []
    pa = br = cu = 0
    for token, _, _ in toks:
        depths.append((pa, br, cu))
        if token == "(": pa += 1
        elif token == ")": pa -= 1
        elif token == "[": br += 1
        elif token == "]": br -= 1
        elif token == "{": cu += 1
        elif token == "}": cu -= 1
    return toks, depths


def ternary_spans(masked: str, *, entry_mode: bool = True) -> tuple[list[Span], list[Span]]:
    """Freeze entry exclusions; recognize unlisted no-space final ternaries."""
    toks, depths = token_depths(masked)
    candidates: list[Span] = []
    exclusions: list[Span] = []
    for i, (token, a, b) in enumerate(toks):
        if token != "?":
            continue
        prev = toks[i - 1][0] if i else ""
        if prev in ("try", "as", "is"):
            exclusions.append(Span(a, b))
            continue
        spaced = a > 0 and b < len(masked) and masked[a - 1].isspace() and masked[b].isspace()
        has_colon = False
        for j in range(i + 1, len(toks)):
            token_j = toks[j][0]
            if depths[j] < depths[i]:
                break
            if depths[j] == depths[i] and token_j == ":":
                has_colon = True
                break
            if depths[j] == depths[i] and token_j in (";", "}"):
                break
        # Entry bytes commit every non-spaced lone question as an exact syntax
        # exclusion. Final bytes first join that frozen exclusion-ID set; an
        # unlisted lone question with a same-depth colon is therefore a new
        # no-space ternary candidate, not a new self-approved exclusion.
        if spaced or (not entry_mode and has_colon):
            candidates.append(Span(a, b))
        else:
            exclusions.append(Span(a, b))
    return candidates, exclusions

def matches_on_line(source: str, starts: list[int], line: int, pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> list[Span]:
    a = starts[line - 1]
    b = starts[line] if line < len(starts) else len(source)
    return [Span(a + m.start(), a + m.end()) for m in pattern.finditer(source[a:b])]


def exclusion_records(path: str) -> list[SyntaxExclusion]:
    source = _source_text(path)
    masked = mask_swift(source)
    starts = line_starts(source)
    decls = declarations(masked)
    spans: list[tuple[str, Span]] = []

    _, question_exclusions = ternary_spans(masked, entry_mode=True)
    spans += [("frozenLoneQuestion", span) for span in question_exclusions]
    spans += [
        ("frozenOptionalChainingDot", Span(match.start(), match.end()))
        for match in re.finditer(r"\?\.", masked)
    ]

    map_pattern = re.compile(r"\.\s*(?:map|flatMap)\b")
    optional_starts: set[int] = set()
    for line in OPTIONAL_LINES.get(path, []):
        matches = matches_on_line(masked, starts, line, map_pattern)
        if not matches:
            raise AssertionError((path, line, "optional map exclusion join not found"))
        optional_starts.add(matches[-1].start)
    for match in map_pattern.finditer(masked):
        if match.start() not in optional_starts:
            spans.append(("collectionMapOrFlatMap", Span(match.start(), match.end())))

    filter_pattern = re.compile(r"\.\s*filter\b")
    drop_filter_starts = {
        match.start() for match in re.finditer(r"\.\s*filter\s*\{", masked)
    }
    drop_filter_starts.update(
        match.start() for match in re.finditer(r"\.\s*filter\s*\(\\\.pinned\)", masked)
    )
    for match in filter_pattern.finditer(masked):
        if match.start() not in drop_filter_starts:
            spans.append(("queryFilter", Span(match.start(), match.end())))

    tokens = [(m.group(0), m.start(), m.end()) for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(masked)]
    records: list[SyntaxExclusion] = []
    for kind, span in spans:
        declaration = declaration_for(decls, span.start)
        overlapping = [i for i, (_, a, b) in enumerate(tokens) if b > span.start and a < span.end]
        first = overlapping[0] if overlapping else next(
            (i for i, (_, a, _) in enumerate(tokens) if a >= span.start), len(tokens) - 1
        )
        last = overlapping[-1] if overlapping else first
        records.append(
            SyntaxExclusion(
                path=path,
                declaration=declaration,
                kind=kind,
                node=" ".join(token for token, _, _ in tokens[first:last + 1]),
                left=" ".join(token for token, _, _ in tokens[max(0, first - 16):first]),
                right=" ".join(token for token, _, _ in tokens[last + 1:last + 17]),
                start=span.start,
            )
        )
    by_window: dict[tuple[str, str, str, str, str, str], list[SyntaxExclusion]] = defaultdict(list)
    for record in records:
        by_window[(record.path, record.declaration, record.kind, record.node, record.left, record.right)].append(record)
    for values in by_window.values():
        values.sort(key=lambda value: value.start)
        for ordinal, record in enumerate(values, 1):
            record.ordinal = ordinal
            serial = "\0".join(
                [record.path, record.declaration, record.kind, record.node, record.left, record.right, str(ordinal)]
            )
            record.digest = sha(serial.encode())
    return records


def collect(path: str) -> list[Occurrence]:
    source = _source_text(path)
    masked = mask_swift(source)
    starts = line_starts(source)
    decls = declarations(masked)
    raw: list[tuple[str, Span]] = []

    raw += [("nilCoalescing", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\?\?", masked)]
    ternaries, question_exclusions = ternary_spans(masked)
    raw += [("ternaryOrSwitchDefault", span) for span in ternaries]
    raw += [("ternaryOrSwitchDefault", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\bdefault\s*:", masked)]
    raw += [("guardEarlyExit", s) for s in guard_exits(masked)]
    raw += [("dropProjection", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\.\s*compactMap\b", masked)]
    raw += [("dropProjection", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\.\s*filter\s*\{", masked)]
    raw += [("dropProjection", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\.\s*filter\s*\(\\\.pinned\)", masked)]
    raw += [("nonthrowingSwallowCatch", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\bcatch\b", masked)]
    # Swift force-try is the lexical token ``try!``.  ``try !predicate`` is a
    # throwing call whose result is then negated and must not be misclassified.
    raw += [("forceTry", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\btry!", masked)]
    raw += [
        ("explicitTrapCall", Span(m.start(), m.end()))
        for m in DIRECT_TRAP_CALL_RE.finditer(masked)
    ]
    raw += [
        ("nonthrowingResultWrapper", Span(m.start(), m.end()))
        for m in NONTHROWING_RESULT_WRAPPER_RE.finditer(masked)
    ]

    map_pattern = re.compile(r"\.\s*(?:map|flatMap)\b")
    for line in OPTIONAL_LINES.get(path, []):
        matches = matches_on_line(masked, starts, line, map_pattern)
        # A line may contain a collection map plus the Optional map. The last
        # projection on each audited line is the Optional/Result candidate.
        if not matches:
            raise AssertionError((path, line, "optional map not found"))
        raw.append(("optionalOrResultProjection", matches[-1]))

    # All entry `_ =` statements are known non-Void calls. Scan them rather
    # than selecting reviewed line numbers so a new explicit discard cannot
    # hide outside the registry.
    explicit_discards = list(re.finditer(r"(?m)^[ \t]*_\s*=", masked))
    raw += [
        ("ignoredNonVoidResult", Span(match.start(), match.end()))
        for match in explicit_discards
    ]
    for line in BARE_NONVOID_LINES.get(path, []):
        a = offset_for_line(starts, line)
        raw.append(("ignoredNonVoidResult", Span(a, a + 1)))
    membership_seen: dict[int, int] = defaultdict(int)
    for line in MEMBERSHIP_LINES.get(path, []):
        matches = matches_on_line(masked, starts, line, re.compile(r"\.(?:insert|remove|removeValue)\s*\("))
        if not matches:
            raise AssertionError((path, line, "membership call not found"))
        # Duplicate line locators consume source-order occurrences.
        index = membership_seen[line]
        membership_seen[line] += 1
        raw.append(("ignoredNonVoidResult", matches[min(index, len(matches)-1)]))
    for line in YIELD_LINES.get(path, []):
        matches = matches_on_line(masked, starts, line, re.compile(r"\.\s*yield\s*\("))
        if not matches:
            raise AssertionError((path, line, "yield not found"))
        raw.append(("ignoredNonVoidResult", matches[0]))

    # max/min/overflow calls are scanned lexically. Three additional business
    # arithmetic anchors are explicit because one lives in SQL string bytes.
    raw += [("businessNumericFallback", Span(m.start(), m.end())) for m in re.finditer(r"\b(?:max|min)\s*\(|\.\s*clamped\b|\.\s*addingReportingOverflow\s*\(", masked)]
    for line, count in NUMERIC_LINES.get(path, []):
        if count == 0:
            continue
        if path.endswith("AppDatabase.swift") and line in (1460, 1505, 1529):
            # Explicit non-lexical aggregate registry. One anchor per row.
            a = offset_for_line(starts, line)
            raw.append(("businessNumericFallback", Span(a, a + 1)))

    tokens = [(m.group(0), m.start(), m.end()) for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(masked)]
    occurrences: list[Occurrence] = []
    for syntax_class, span in raw:
        declaration = declaration_for(decls, span.start)
        overlapping = [i for i, (_, a, b) in enumerate(tokens) if b > span.start and a < span.end]
        if overlapping:
            first, last = overlapping[0], overlapping[-1]
        else:
            first = next((i for i, (_, a, _) in enumerate(tokens) if a >= span.start), len(tokens) - 1)
            last = first
        node = " ".join(t[0] for t in tokens[first:last + 1])
        left = " ".join(t[0] for t in tokens[max(0, first - 16):first])
        right = " ".join(t[0] for t in tokens[last + 1:last + 17])
        occurrences.append(Occurrence(path, declaration, syntax_class, span.start, span.end, node, left, right))

    by_window: dict[tuple[str, str, str, str, str, str], list[Occurrence]] = defaultdict(list)
    for o in occurrences:
        by_window[(o.path, o.declaration, o.syntax_class, o.node, o.left, o.right)].append(o)
    for values in by_window.values():
        values.sort(key=lambda x: x.start)
        for ordinal, o in enumerate(values, 1):
            o.ordinal = ordinal
            serial = "\0".join([o.path, o.declaration, o.syntax_class, o.node, o.left, o.right, str(ordinal)])
            o.digest = sha(serial.encode())
    return occurrences


def self_probes() -> None:
    # The entry bytes intentionally freeze every pre-existing unspaced lone
    # question as an exclusion. A newly injected no-space ternary is still a
    # candidate in final mode, so whitespace cannot evade the gate.
    no_space = mask_swift("let z=a?b:c\n")
    entry_candidates, entry_exclusions = ternary_spans(no_space, entry_mode=True)
    final_candidates, _ = ternary_spans(no_space, entry_mode=False)
    assert len(entry_candidates) == 0 and len(entry_exclusions) == 1
    assert len(final_candidates) == 1
    spaced_candidates, _ = ternary_spans(mask_swift("let z = a ? b : c\n"))
    assert len(spaced_candidates) == 1

    # Raw-string hash count is deliberately unbounded; interpolation remains
    # code while ordinary contents (including fake candidates) are masked.
    raw = '##########"x ?? y \\##########(a ?? b)"##########\n'
    masked_raw = mask_swift(raw)
    assert len(re.findall(r"\?\?", masked_raw)) == 1
    try:
        mask_swift('"illegal\nnewline"')
    except ValueError as error:
        assert "unescaped newline" in str(error)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("single-line string newline was accepted")

    nested = mask_swift("/* outer /* a ?? b */ still */ let x = c ?? d\n")
    assert len(re.findall(r"\?\?", nested)) == 1

    traps = mask_swift(
        "fatalError()\npreconditionFailure()\nprecondition(false)\n"
        "assertionFailure()\nassert(false)\nabort()\nexit(1)\n_exit(1)\n"
    )
    assert len(list(DIRECT_TRAP_CALL_RE.finditer(traps))) == 8
    wrappers = mask_swift("let a = Result(catching: work)\nlet b = Result { try body() }\n")
    assert len(list(NONTHROWING_RESULT_WRAPPER_RE.finditer(wrappers))) == 2
    force_try_fixture = mask_swift("let a = try! make()\nlet b = try !predicate()\n")
    assert len(list(re.finditer(r"\btry!", force_try_fixture))) == 1

    optional_type = mask_swift("let value: String? = nil\n")
    type_tokens, type_depths = token_depths(optional_type)
    type_index = next(i for i, item in enumerate(type_tokens) if item[0] == "?")
    assert _deterministic_question_exclusion(
        optional_type, type_tokens, type_depths, type_index
    ) == "proven-optional-type-postfix"

    def question_fixture(
        text: str,
    ) -> list[tuple[str | None, bool]]:
        fixture = mask_swift(text)
        fixture_tokens, fixture_depths = token_depths(fixture)
        return [
            (
                _deterministic_question_exclusion(
                    fixture, fixture_tokens, fixture_depths, index
                ),
                _same_depth_colon(
                    fixture, fixture_tokens, fixture_depths, index
                ),
            )
            for index, item in enumerate(fixture_tokens)
            if item[0] == "?"
        ]

    proven_optional = "proven-optional-type-postfix"
    assert question_fixture(
        "let first: String?\nlet second: Int?\n"
    ) == [(proven_optional, False), (proven_optional, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "var first: String? = nil\nvar second: Int? = nil\n"
    ) == [(proven_optional, False), (proven_optional, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "private var token: NSObjectProtocol?\nfunc install() {}\n"
    ) == [(proven_optional, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "protocol Source {\n"
        "func read(value: String?) -> String?\nfunc close()\n}\n"
    ) == [(proven_optional, False), (proven_optional, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "enum Item {\ncase value(label: String?)\n}\n"
    ) == [(proven_optional, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "let selected = condition\n    ? first\n    : second\n"
    ) == [(None, True)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "let selected = condition ?\n    first :\n    second\n"
    ) == [(None, True)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "let selected = condition ?\n"
        "    if ready {\n        first\n    } else {\n        second\n    }\n"
        "    : fallback\n"
    ) == [(None, True)]
    # A call label is not declaration evidence.  With no grammatical type
    # delimiter, its tight question remains unresolved instead of borrowing
    # the later ternary colon.
    assert question_fixture(
