        "consume(value: condition?\n    yes : no)\n"
    ) == [(None, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "consume(prefix, value: condition?\n    yes : no)\n"
    ) == [(None, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "let declared: Int\nconsume(value: condition?\n    yes : no)\n"
    ) == [(None, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "let closure = { () -> Bool in\n"
        "    consume(value: condition?)\n}\n"
    ) == [(None, False)]
    assert question_fixture(
        "switch item {\ncase .some(value: item?): break\n}\n"
    ) == [(None, False)]
    # An unresolved postfix question at a physical statement boundary cannot
    # consume a colon from the next declaration.
    assert question_fixture(
        "let unresolved = value?\nlet label: String\n"
    ) == [(None, False)]

    for text in (
        "value?.name\n", "value?[0]\n", "value?()\n",
        "value as? String\n", "switch value { case item?: break }\n",
    ):
        projected = mask_swift(text)
        projected_tokens = [
            (m.group(), m.start(), m.end()) for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(projected)
        ]
        if any(item[0] == "?" for item in projected_tokens):
            index = next(i for i, item in enumerate(projected_tokens) if item[0] == "?")
            _, projected_depths = token_depths(projected)
            assert _deterministic_question_exclusion(
                projected, projected_tokens, projected_depths, index
            ) is None

    assert len(planned_manifest_by_id()) == 17
    sample_entry = "EF-E-" + "1" * 64
    sample_final = "EF-F-" + "2" * 64
    assert RESOLVE_RE.fullmatch(
        f" P1-B-RESOLVE KEEP {sample_entry} {sample_final}"
    )
    assert not RESOLVE_RE.fullmatch(
        f" P1-B-RESOLVE {sample_entry} retained {sample_final} deadbeef x"
    )
    terminal_v2_self_probes()


def load_classifications(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    result: dict[str, str] = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: expected EntryOccurrenceID<TAB>Classification")
        occurrence_id, classification = fields
        if not re.fullmatch(r"EF-E-[0-9a-f]{64}", occurrence_id):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: invalid EntryOccurrenceID")
        harmless = re.fullmatch(r"harmless:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*", classification)
        refs = classification.split("+")
        semantic_tag = r"[A-Z]+\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:,\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*\]"
        ref_pattern = re.compile(
            r"(?:descriptor:N\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+\]:(?:typed|capture|approved-residual)|"
            rf"cross:(?:literal|catch|raw):{semantic_tag})"
        )
        valid_ref_set = (
            all(ref_pattern.fullmatch(ref) for ref in refs)
            and refs == sorted(set(refs))
        )
        if not harmless and not valid_ref_set:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: invalid ClassificationSet {classification!r}")
        if occurrence_id in result:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: duplicate {occurrence_id}")
        result[occurrence_id] = classification
    return result


def load_n_registry(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    result: dict[str, str] = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) < 2 or not re.fullmatch(r"N\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+\]", fields[0]):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: invalid N registry row")
        if fields[1] not in ("typed", "capture", "approved-residual"):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: invalid N disposition")
        if fields[0] in result:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: duplicate N tag")
        result[fields[0]] = fields[1]
    dispositions = defaultdict(int)
    for disposition in result.values():
        dispositions[disposition] += 1
    if len(result) != 130 or dict(dispositions) != {
        "typed": 89,
        "capture": 14,
        "approved-residual": 27,
    }:
        raise ValueError(("N registry checksum", len(result), dict(dispositions)))
    return result


def validate_standalone_census(
    path: Path, occurrence_by_id: dict[str, Occurrence]
) -> tuple[list[str], str]:
    census_ids: set[str] = set()
    reviewed: set[str] = set()
    exclusions: list[str] = []
    explicit = bare = 0
    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 10:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: malformed standalone census row")
        census_id, _, _, statement_kind, classification, reviewed_id, *_ = fields
        if census_id in census_ids:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: duplicate census ID {census_id}")
        census_ids.add(census_id)
        if classification == "reviewedIgnoredNonVoid":
            if not reviewed_id or reviewed_id in reviewed:
                raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: invalid reviewed join {reviewed_id}")
            reviewed.add(reviewed_id)
            explicit += statement_kind == "explicitDiscard"
            bare += statement_kind == "standaloneCall"
        elif classification == "unreviewedStandaloneCallSyntax":
            if reviewed_id or not census_id.startswith("SC-X-"):
                raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: invalid syntax exclusion")
            exclusions.append(census_id)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: unknown standalone classification")
    expected_reviewed = {
        occurrence_id
        for occurrence_id, occurrence in occurrence_by_id.items()
        if occurrence.syntax_class == "ignoredNonVoidResult"
    }
    if reviewed != expected_reviewed or (len(census_ids), len(exclusions), explicit, bare) != (
        2279,
        2199,
        17,
        63,
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            ("standalone census checksum", len(census_ids), len(reviewed), len(exclusions), explicit, bare)
        )
    ids = sorted(exclusions)
    serial = "\0".join(["StandaloneCallSyntaxExclusionRegistryV1", *ids])
    digest = sha(serial.encode())
    if digest != "546d71040b0c73d655c3de30fdb7354f9fd933122579715a2c43ad36956b047b":
        raise ValueError(("standalone exclusion digest", digest))
    return ids, digest


def validate_n_coverage(
    path: Path,
    classifications: dict[str, str],
    n_registry: dict[str, str],
) -> None:
    expected: dict[str, tuple[str, set[str]]] = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 4:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: malformed N coverage row")
        tag, disposition, count_text, ids_text = fields
        ids = set(filter(None, ids_text.split(",")))
        if tag in expected or int(count_text) != len(ids):
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: duplicate/count mismatch")
        expected[tag] = (disposition, ids)
    if {tag: disposition for tag, (disposition, _) in expected.items()} != n_registry:
        raise ValueError("N coverage registry/disposition mismatch")
    actual: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for occurrence_id, classification in classifications.items():
        for tag, disposition in re.findall(
            r"descriptor:(N\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+\]):(typed|capture|approved-residual)", classification
        ):
            if n_registry.get(tag) != disposition:
                raise ValueError(("wrong N disposition", occurrence_id, tag, disposition))
            actual[tag].add(occurrence_id)
    for tag, (_, ids) in expected.items():
        if actual.get(tag, set()) != ids:
            raise ValueError(("N occurrence coverage mismatch", tag, actual.get(tag, set()), ids))


def validate_cross_coverage(
    path: Path,
    gate_registry_path: Path,
    classifications: dict[str, str],
    occurrence_by_id: dict[str, Occurrence],
) -> None:
    allowed_gate_tags: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for number, line in enumerate(gate_registry_path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 2 or fields[0] not in ("literal", "catch", "raw"):
            raise ValueError(f"{gate_registry_path}:{number}: malformed gate/tag row")
        row = (fields[0], fields[1])
        if row in allowed_gate_tags:
            raise ValueError(f"{gate_registry_path}:{number}: duplicate gate/tag row")
        allowed_gate_tags.add(row)
    gate_counts = Counter(gate for gate, _ in allowed_gate_tags)
    if gate_counts != Counter({"literal": 134, "catch": 134}):
        raise ValueError(("gate/tag registry checksum", gate_counts))
    expected: set[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] = set()
    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 5:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: malformed cross coverage row")
        row = tuple(fields)
        if row in expected:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: duplicate cross row")
        expected.add(row)
    actual: set[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] = set()
    semantic_tag = r"[A-Z]+\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:,\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*\]"
    for occurrence_id, classification in classifications.items():
        occurrence = occurrence_by_id[occurrence_id]
        for gate, tag in re.findall(rf"cross:(literal|catch|raw):({semantic_tag})", classification):
            if (gate, tag) not in allowed_gate_tags:
                raise ValueError(("unknown or wrong-gate cross ref", occurrence_id, gate, tag))
            actual.add((occurrence_id, occurrence.path, occurrence.declaration, gate, tag))
    if actual != expected:
        raise ValueError(("cross coverage mismatch", len(actual), len(expected), sorted(actual - expected)[:3], sorted(expected - actual)[:3]))
    catch_ids = {
        occurrence_id
        for occurrence_id, occurrence in occurrence_by_id.items()
        if occurrence.syntax_class == "nonthrowingSwallowCatch"
    }
    joined_entry_catches = [
        occurrence_id
        for occurrence_id, _, _, gate, tag in actual
        if gate == "catch"
        and tag.startswith("E[")
        and occurrence_by_id[occurrence_id].syntax_class == "nonthrowingSwallowCatch"
    ]
    catch_ref_counts = Counter(joined_entry_catches)
    duplicate_catch_refs = sorted(
        occurrence_id for occurrence_id, count in catch_ref_counts.items() if count != 1
    )
    if (
        catch_ids != set(joined_entry_catches)
        or duplicate_catch_refs
        or len(joined_entry_catches) != 134
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            (
                "catch cross join is not one-to-one",
                len(catch_ids),
                len(joined_entry_catches),
                duplicate_catch_refs[:3],
            )
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Standalone call-root grammar (inlined; no external helper dependency)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CALL_PREFIX = r"(?:(?:try\s*[!?]?|await|consume|copy|borrowing)\s+)"
CALL_ATOM = r"\.?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*"
CALL_MEMBER = r"(?:\s*[!?]?\s*\.\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)*"
CALL_HEAD_RE = re.compile(
    rf"(?<![A-Za-z_0-9.])(?P<prefix>{CALL_PREFIX}*)"
    rf"(?P<callee>{CALL_ATOM}{CALL_MEMBER})\s*(?P<opening>\(|\{{)"
)
CALL_REJECT_FIRST = {
    "if", "guard", "while", "for", "switch", "return", "throw", "let",
    "var", "case", "default", "func", "init", "deinit", "subscript",
    "actor", "class", "struct", "enum", "extension", "protocol", "catch",
    "else", "do", "defer", "repeat", "import", "break", "continue", "get",
    "set", "willSet", "didSet", "in", "where", "associatedtype", "typealias",
}


@dataclass
class CallRoot:
    path: str
    declaration: str
    statement_kind: str
    start: int
    significant: int
    end: int
    node: str
    left: str
    right: str
    reviewed_id: str = ""
    ordinal: int = 0
    digest: str = ""


def _line_end(source: str, pos: int) -> int:
    end = source.find("\n", pos)
    return len(source) if end < 0 else end


def _previous_significant(source: str, pos: int, floor: int) -> str:
    pos -= 1
    while pos >= floor and source[pos].isspace():
        pos -= 1
    return source[pos] if pos >= floor else ""


def _next_nonblank_line(source: str, pos: int) -> str:
    while pos < len(source):
        end = _line_end(source, pos)
        line = source[pos:end].strip()
        if line:
            return line
        pos = end + 1
    return ""


def _statement_end(masked: str, significant: int, line_floor: int) -> int:
    pa = br = cu = 0
    i = significant
    while i < len(masked):
        c = masked[i]
        if c == "(": pa += 1
        elif c == ")":
            if pa: pa -= 1
        elif c == "[": br += 1
        elif c == "]":
            if br: br -= 1
        elif c == "{": cu += 1
        elif c == "}":
            if cu: cu -= 1
            elif pa == br == 0: return i
        elif c == ";" and pa == br == cu == 0:
            return i
        elif c == "\n" and pa == br == cu == 0:
            before = _previous_significant(masked, i, line_floor)
            nxt = _next_nonblank_line(masked, i + 1)
            continuation = (
                before in ".,=:+-*/%&|?\\"
                or nxt.startswith((".", "?.", "!."))
                or bool(re.match(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\s*:\s*\{", nxt))
            )
            if not continuation:
                return i
        i += 1
    return len(masked)


def _top_level_sequence_operator(masked: str, significant: int, end: int) -> bool:
    pa = br = cu = 0
    i = significant
    while i < end:
        c = masked[i]
        if c == "(": pa += 1
        elif c == ")" and pa: pa -= 1
        elif c == "[": br += 1
        elif c == "]" and br: br -= 1
        elif c == "{": cu += 1
        elif c == "}" and cu: cu -= 1
        elif pa == br == cu == 0:
            pair = masked[i:i + 2]
            if pair in ("??", "==", "!=", "<=", ">=", "&&", "||", "+=", "-=", "*=", "/=", "%="):
                return True
            if c == "=" or c == ":": return True
            if c == "?" and pair != "?.": return True
            if c in "+-*/%&|<>": return True
        i += 1
    return False


def _make_call_root(
    path: str,
    masked: str,
    decls: list[tuple[int, int, str]],
    start: int,
    significant: int,
    end: int,
    kind: str,
    trigger: tuple[int, int],
    tokens: list[tuple[str, int, int]],
) -> CallRoot:
    ta, tb = trigger
    overlap = [i for i, (_, a, b) in enumerate(tokens) if b > ta and a < tb]
    if not overlap:
        raise AssertionError((path, ta, "no call-root trigger tokens"))
    first, last = overlap[0], overlap[-1]
    return CallRoot(
        path=path,
        declaration=declaration_for(decls, significant),
        statement_kind=kind,
        start=start,
        significant=significant,
        end=end,
        node=" ".join(item[0] for item in tokens[first:last + 1]),
        left=" ".join(item[0] for item in tokens[max(0, first - 16):first]),
        right=" ".join(item[0] for item in tokens[last + 1:last + 17]),
    )


def call_root_rows(path: str) -> list[CallRoot]:
    source = _source_text(path)
    masked = mask_swift(source)
    decls = declarations(masked)
    tokens = [(m.group(), m.start(), m.end()) for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(masked)]
    pa = br = 0
    brace_stack: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
    states: list[tuple[int, int, tuple[int, int]]] = []
    for c in masked:
        states.append((pa, br, brace_stack[-1] if brace_stack else (0, 0)))
        if c == "(": pa += 1
        elif c == ")": pa -= 1
        elif c == "[": br += 1
        elif c == "]": br -= 1
        elif c == "{": brace_stack.append((pa, br))
        elif c == "}" and brace_stack: brace_stack.pop()
        if pa < 0 or br < 0:
            raise AssertionError((path, "delimiter underflow"))
    if pa or br or brace_stack:
        raise AssertionError((path, "unterminated delimiter", pa, br, len(brace_stack)))

    rows: list[CallRoot] = []
    for head in CALL_HEAD_RE.finditer(masked):
        significant = head.start()
        floor = masked.rfind("\n", 0, significant) + 1
        first = floor + len(masked[floor:significant]) - len(masked[floor:significant].lstrip())
        prev = significant - 1
        while prev >= floor and masked[prev] in " \t":
            prev -= 1
        pa, br, base = states[significant]
        at_scope_level = (pa, br) == base
        at_line_start = significant == first
        after_delimiter = prev >= 0 and masked[prev] in "{;" and at_scope_level
        if not (after_delimiter or (at_line_start and at_scope_level)):
            continue
        if at_line_start and head.group("callee").startswith("."):
            continue
        first_word = re.match(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*", head.group("callee").lstrip("."))
        if first_word and first_word.group() in CALL_REJECT_FIRST:
            continue
        end = _statement_end(masked, significant, floor)
        text = masked[significant:end].rstrip()
        if text and text[-1] in ")}" and not _top_level_sequence_operator(masked, significant, end):
            rows.append(_make_call_root(
                path, masked, decls, floor, significant, end, "standaloneCall",
                (head.start(), head.end()), tokens,
            ))

    for match in re.finditer(r"(?m)^[ \t]*_\s*=", masked):
        floor = match.start()
        significant = floor + len(masked[floor:match.end()]) - len(masked[floor:match.end()].lstrip())
        end = _statement_end(masked, significant, floor)
        trigger = (match.start() + len(match.group()) - len(match.group().lstrip()), match.end())
        rows.append(_make_call_root(
            path, masked, decls, floor, significant, end, "explicitDiscard", trigger, tokens,
        ))
    return rows


def finalize_call_roots(rows: list[CallRoot]) -> None:
    buckets: dict[tuple[str, ...], list[CallRoot]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        buckets[(row.path, row.declaration, row.statement_kind, row.node, row.left, row.right)].append(row)
    for values in buckets.values():
        values.sort(key=lambda value: value.significant)
        for ordinal, row in enumerate(values, 1):
            row.ordinal = ordinal
            serial = "\0".join([
                row.path, row.declaration, row.statement_kind, row.node,
                row.left, row.right, str(ordinal),
            ])
            row.digest = sha(serial.encode())


def join_entry_reviewed_roots(
    rows: list[CallRoot], reviewed_occurrences: list[Occurrence]
) -> None:
    unmatched: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
    for occurrence in reviewed_occurrences:
        source = _source_text(occurrence.path)
        physical_start = source.rfind("\n", 0, occurrence.start) + 1
        bare_anchor = (
            occurrence.start == physical_start
            and not source[physical_start:].lstrip().startswith("_")
        )
        matches: list[CallRoot] = []
        if bare_anchor:
            occurrence_line = source.count("\n", 0, occurrence.start)
            matches = [
                row for row in rows
                if row.path == occurrence.path
                and row.statement_kind == "standaloneCall"
                and source.count("\n", 0, row.significant) == occurrence_line
                and row.declaration == occurrence.declaration
            ]
            if not matches:
                matches = [
                    row for row in rows
                    if row.path == occurrence.path
                    and row.statement_kind == "standaloneCall"
                    and row.significant <= occurrence.start < row.end
                    and row.declaration == occurrence.declaration
                ]
        else:
            for row in rows:
                if row.path != occurrence.path:
                    continue
                if row.statement_kind == "explicitDiscard":
                    if row.start <= occurrence.start < row.end:
                        matches.append(row)
                elif row.significant <= occurrence.start < row.end:
                    matches.append(row)
        matches = list({id(row): row for row in matches}.values())
        if len(matches) != 1 and matches:
            width = min(row.end - row.significant for row in matches)
            matches = [row for row in matches if row.end - row.significant == width]
        if len(matches) != 1:
            unmatched.append((occurrence.path, occurrence.declaration, occurrence.start, len(matches)))
            continue
        row = matches[0]
        if row.reviewed_id:
            clone = CallRoot(**row.__dict__)
            clone.start = occurrence.start
            clone.significant = occurrence.start
            clone.reviewed_id = ""
            rows.append(clone)
            row = clone
        row.reviewed_id = "EF-E-" + occurrence.digest
    if unmatched:
        raise AssertionError(("unmatched reviewed call roots", unmatched[:20], len(unmatched)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Frozen inline-annex parser and orthogonal classification closure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

HARmless_RE = re.compile(r"harmless:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*")
SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN = r"[A-Z]+\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+(?:,\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)*\]"
REFERENCE_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:descriptor:N\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+\]:(?:typed|capture|approved-residual)|"
    rf"cross:(?:literal|catch|raw):{SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})"
)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FrozenEntry:
    occurrence_id: str
    path: str
    declaration: str
    syntax_class: str
    classification: str
    group_digest: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FrozenExclusion:
    exclusion_id: str
    path: str
    declaration: str
    exclusion_class: str
    node_kind: str
    node: str
    left: str
    right: str
    ordinal: int


@dataclass
class FrozenInventory:
    entries: dict[str, FrozenEntry]
    exclusions: dict[str, FrozenExclusion]
    n_coverage: dict[str, tuple[str, frozenset[str]]]
    cross_coverage: frozenset[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]]
    gate_tags: frozenset[tuple[str, str]]
    primary_seams: dict[str, str]
    catch_dispositions: dict[str, str]
    delegate_registry: dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]]

    @property
    def business_ids(self) -> set[str]:
        return {
            ident for ident, row in self.entries.items()
            if not row.classification.startswith("harmless:")
        }

    @property
    def harmless_ids(self) -> set[str]:
        return set(self.entries) - self.business_ids

    @property
    def core_exclusion_ids(self) -> set[str]:
        return {ident for ident in self.exclusions if ident.startswith("SX-E-")}

    @property
    def standalone_exclusion_ids(self) -> set[str]:
        return {ident for ident in self.exclusions if ident.startswith("SC-X-")}


def _fenced_annex(document: str, heading: str) -> str:
    matches = list(re.finditer(
        rf"(?m)^{re.escape(heading)}$", document,
    ))
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise ValueError((heading, "inline annex heading cardinality", len(matches)))
    start = matches[0].start()
    opening = document.find("```tsv\n", start)
    if opening < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"missing TSV fence after {heading}")
    opening += len("```tsv\n")
    closing = document.find("\n```", opening)
    if closing < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"unterminated TSV fence after {heading}")
    # Canonical fenced payload includes its final LF but excludes the closing
    # fence. This is the byte sequence committed by the five annex hashes.
    return document[opening:closing + 1]


def validate_classification_set(classification: str) -> None:
    harmless = HARmless_RE.fullmatch(classification)
    refs = classification.split("+")
    valid_refs = (
        all(REFERENCE_RE.fullmatch(ref) for ref in refs)
        and refs == sorted(set(refs))
    )
    if bool(harmless) == bool(valid_refs):
        raise ValueError(f"classification is not one orthogonal closed set: {classification!r}")


def _markdown_cells(line: str) -> list[str]:
    return [cell.strip() for cell in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]


_EXECUTION_ONLY_SEAM_ROWS = (
    (
        "mcpFinishServerCleanup",
        "McpWorkflowController.finishServerCleanup(_:)",
        "Sources/AgentLoopApp/McpStore.swift",
        "McpStore.retryServerCleanup(serverId:)",
        "MCP4 internal cleanup table",
    ),
    (
        "schedulePostCommitRepair",
        "MissionWorkflowController.retrySchedulePostCommit(_:registration:notifications:)",
        "Sources/AgentLoopApp/AppStore.swift",
        "AppStore.retrySchedulePostCommit(key:)",
        "A13 internal committed-visibility table",
    ),
)


def _execution_only_seam_rows(
    document: str,
) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, str, str], ...]:
    """Parse the exact closed §9.2 table; prose or code literals are not authority."""
    heading = "### 9." + "2 Planned execution-only seam ledger (2)"
    lines = document.splitlines()
    headings = [index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if line == heading]
    if len(headings) != 1:
        raise ValueError(("§9.2 execution-only heading cardinality", len(headings)))
    start = headings[0]
    end = next((
        index for index in range(start + 1, len(lines))
        if lines[index].startswith("#")
    ), len(lines))
    section = lines[start + 1:end]
    header = "| ProductionFailureSeam | Exact production callable / delegate | Executed owner |"
    headers = [index for index, line in enumerate(section) if line == header]
    if len(headers) != 1:
        raise ValueError(("§9.2 execution-only table header cardinality", len(headers)))
    header_index = headers[0]
    if (
        header_index + 1 >= len(section)
        or section[header_index + 1] != "|---|---|---|"
    ):
        raise ValueError("§9.2 execution-only table separator")
    raw_rows: list[list[str]] = []
    for line in section[header_index + 2:]:
        if not line.startswith("|"):
            break
        cells = _markdown_cells(line)
        if len(cells) != 3:
            raise ValueError(("§9.2 execution-only row width", cells))
        raw_rows.append(cells)
    parsed: list[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] = []
    for cells in raw_rows:
        seam_match = re.fullmatch(r"`([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`", cells[0])
        callable_delegate = re.fullmatch(
            r"callable `([^`]+)`; delegate `([^`]+)::([^`]+)`", cells[1]
        )
        owner_match = re.fullmatch(r"`([^`]+)` (.+)", cells[2])
        if seam_match is None or callable_delegate is None or owner_match is None:
            raise ValueError(("§9.2 execution-only row grammar", cells))
        parsed.append((
            seam_match.group(1), callable_delegate.group(1),
            callable_delegate.group(2), callable_delegate.group(3),
            owner_match.group(1) + " " + owner_match.group(2),
        ))
    result = tuple(parsed)
    if result != _EXECUTION_ONLY_SEAM_ROWS:
        raise ValueError(("§9.2 execution-only closed rows", result))
    return result


def _descriptor_registries(document: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, str]]:
    """Expand entry descriptors plus the exact fourteen planned N rows."""
    seams: dict[str, str] = {}
    lines = document.splitlines()
    table_mode = ""
    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith("| Tags | Primary seam |"):
            table_mode = "tag-seam"
            continue
        if line.startswith("| Tag | Entry bypass | Terminal | Operation / ProductionFailureSeam |"):
            table_mode = "n-seam"
            continue
        if line.startswith("| Planned path | Disposition/tag | Primary seam |"):
            table_mode = "planned-n-seam"
            continue
        if not line.startswith("|"):
            table_mode = ""
            continue
        if re.fullmatch(r"\|?[\s|:\-]+\|?", line):
            continue
        cells = _markdown_cells(line)
        if table_mode == "tag-seam" and len(cells) >= 2:
            seam = cells[1].strip("`")
            for tag in re.findall(rf"`({SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})`", cells[0]):
                if seam == "none" or tag in seams:
                    if tag in seams:
                        raise ValueError(("duplicate descriptor tag", tag))
                    continue
                seams[tag] = seam
        elif table_mode == "n-seam" and len(cells) >= 4:
            match = re.fullmatch(rf"`({SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})`", cells[0])
            if match is None:
                continue
            values = [part.strip().strip("`") for part in cells[3].split("/")]
            if len(values) < 2 or not re.fullmatch(
                r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", values[-1]
            ):
                raise ValueError(("N descriptor primary seam", cells[0], cells[3]))
            tag = match.group(1)
            if tag in seams:
                raise ValueError(("duplicate descriptor tag", tag))
            seams[tag] = values[-1]
        elif table_mode == "planned-n-seam" and len(cells) >= 3:
            match = re.search(rf"({SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})", cells[1])
            seam = cells[2].strip("`")
            if match is None or not re.fullmatch(
                r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", seam
            ):
                raise ValueError(("planned N descriptor row", cells[:3]))
            tag = match.group(1)
            if tag in seams:
                raise ValueError(("duplicate planned descriptor tag", tag))
            seams[tag] = seam
    catch_dispositions: dict[str, str] = {}
    in_catch_inventory = False
    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith("### 8.1 Core entry catches"):
            in_catch_inventory = True
            continue
        if line.startswith("### 8.5 Catch descriptor"):
            in_catch_inventory = False
        if not in_catch_inventory or not line.startswith("|"):
            continue
        tag_match = re.search(rf"`({SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})`\s*\|\s*$", line)
        disposition_match = re.search(r"\|\s*`([TAC])`(?:\s*:|\s*\|)", line)
        if tag_match is None or disposition_match is None:
            continue
        disposition = {
            "T": "typed", "A": "approved-residual", "C": "capture",
        }[disposition_match.group(1)]
        tag = tag_match.group(1)
        if tag in catch_dispositions:
            raise ValueError(("duplicate catch disposition", tag))
        catch_dispositions[tag] = disposition

    for seam, _, _, _, _ in _execution_only_seam_rows(document):
        key = "execution-only:" + seam
        if key in seams or seam in seams.values():
            raise ValueError(("duplicate §9.2 execution-only seam", seam))
        seams[key] = seam

    if len(seams) != 411:
        raise ValueError(("descriptor primary-seam registry", len(seams), 411))
    if len(catch_dispositions) != 134:
        raise ValueError(("catch disposition registry", len(catch_dispositions), 134))
    return seams, catch_dispositions


def _closed_planned_table(document: str) -> tuple[tuple[str, str, str, str, str], ...]:
    anchor = "The closed final-only tuple registry is:"
    start = document.find(anchor)
    if start < 0:
        raise ValueError("planned tuple table missing")
    lines = document[start:].splitlines()
    header_index = next((
        index for index, line in enumerate(lines)
        if line.startswith("| Final path | Canonical DeclarationID |")
    ), -1)
    if header_index < 0:
        raise ValueError("planned tuple header missing")
    rows: list[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] = []
    for line in lines[header_index + 2:]:
        if not line.startswith("|"):
            break
        cells = _markdown_cells(line)
        if len(cells) != 6 or cells[5] != "1":
            raise ValueError(("planned tuple table row", cells))
        rows.append(tuple(cell.strip("`") for cell in cells[:5]))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    result = tuple(rows)
    if result != PLANNED_MANIFEST:
        raise ValueError(("planned tuple authority/order drift", result, PLANNED_MANIFEST))
    return result


def _delegate_registry(document: str) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Derive the exact DE-001...DE-127 tuple registry from authority tables."""
    tuples: set[tuple[str, str, str]] = set()
    header: list[str] = []
    for line in document.splitlines():
        if not line.startswith("|"):
            header = []
            continue
        cells = _markdown_cells(line)
        if (
            any("Delegate edge" in cell for cell in cells)
            or (
                "Exact App path::containing declaration" in cells
                and ("Direct seam" in cells or "Additional direct seam" in cells)
            )
        ):
            header = cells
            continue
        if not header or re.fullmatch(r"\|?[\s|:\-]+\|?", line):
            continue
        if "Delegate edge" in header:
            delegate_cell = cells[header.index("Delegate edge")]
            if delegate_cell == "none":
                continue
            default_seam = cells[header.index("Primary seam")].strip("`")
        else:
            delegate_cell = cells[
                header.index("Exact App path::containing declaration")
            ]
            seam_header = (
                "Direct seam" if "Direct seam" in header
                else "Additional direct seam"
            )
            default_seam = cells[header.index(seam_header)].strip("`")
        matches = list(re.finditer(
            r"Sources/AgentLoopApp/[A-Za-z0-9_/]+\.swift::",
            delegate_cell,
        ))
        for index, match in enumerate(matches):
            end = matches[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(matches) else len(delegate_cell)
            segment = delegate_cell[match.start():end]
            # Cells separate multiple tuples with <br> or distinct code spans.
            segment = re.split(r"<br>|`;|`\s*\(", segment)[0]
            override = re.search(
                r"\s+=>\s+`?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", segment
            )
            raw = segment[:override.start()] if override else segment
            path, declaration = raw.strip("` ;").split("::", 1)
            seam = override.group(1) if override else default_seam
            if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", seam):
                raise ValueError(("delegate seam", seam, segment))
            tuples.add((path, declaration, seam))
    for seam, _, path, declaration, _ in _execution_only_seam_rows(document):
        execution_tuple = (path, declaration, seam)
        if execution_tuple in tuples:
            raise ValueError(("duplicate §9.2 DelegateEdge tuple", execution_tuple))
        tuples.add(execution_tuple)
    ordered = sorted(tuples, key=lambda row: "\0".join(row))
    if len(ordered) != 127:
        raise ValueError(("DelegateEdge tuple union", len(ordered), 127))
    return {
        f"DE-{index:03d}": row for index, row in enumerate(ordered, 1)
    }


def _validate_terminal_authority(document: str) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]]:
    _closed_planned_table(document)
    required_arithmetic = (
        "planned-new-catch N rows          14 =  6 typed +  7 capture +  1 approved",
        "descriptor rows                  413 = 133 + 134 + 130 + 14 + 2",
        "production descriptors           411",
        "production invocation variants   416",
        "DelegateEdge tuple union          127 (DE-001...DE-127)",
    )
    missing = [line for line in required_arithmetic if line not in document]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(("terminal authority arithmetic drift", missing))
    return _delegate_registry(document)


def load_frozen_inventory_document(document: str) -> FrozenInventory:
    primary_seams, catch_dispositions = _descriptor_registries(document)
    delegate_registry = _validate_terminal_authority(document)
    group_text = _fenced_annex(
        document, "#### §9.1b Inline classification-aware group appendix (954 occurrences)"
    )
    annex_hashes = {
        "groups": (group_text, "e505406b23fa633e776e198da0e71fb94c407453b0151da090b2e5dd95e43b2e"),
        "n": (_fenced_annex(document, "#### §9.1c Inline N occurrence coverage (130 tags)"), "272d6cfc205b9a11f206c91fe7c0a47514b698e599925ae123837fa25da12d22"),
        "cross": (_fenced_annex(document, "#### §9.1d Inline cross-gate occurrence coverage (248 tuples)"), "bdf700d7779b0eed6d2ac2639b44788cd9f712e744bd60d6e3d68f1a1f816019"),
        "gate": (_fenced_annex(document, "#### §9.1e Inline literal/catch semantic-tag registry"), "107fe79d430b699c23b958f071b494484002b3da9bb3ace55a70d62aede5547d"),
        "exclusions": (_fenced_annex(document, "#### §9.1f Inline expanded syntax-exclusion appendix (2,962 IDs)"), "c37f56791dace7aba0e118960def7c8e56a0bd402b4728c12a79288b84482cf3"),
    }
    for name, (payload, expected_hash) in annex_hashes.items():
        actual_hash = sha(payload.encode())
        if actual_hash != expected_hash:
            raise ValueError(("frozen annex byte drift", name, expected_hash, actual_hash))
    entries: dict[str, FrozenEntry] = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(group_text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 7:
            raise ValueError(f"group annex row {number}: expected 7 TSV fields")
        count_text, source_path, declaration, syntax_class, classification, digest, ids_text = fields
        validate_classification_set(classification)
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", digest):
            raise ValueError(f"group annex row {number}: invalid groupDigest")
        ids = ids_text.split(",")
        if ids != sorted(set(ids)) or int(count_text) != len(ids):
            raise ValueError(f"group annex row {number}: count/order/uniqueness mismatch")
        if not all(re.fullmatch(r"EF-E-[0-9a-f]{64}", ident) for ident in ids):
            raise ValueError(f"group annex row {number}: malformed entry occurrence ID")
        serial = "\0".join([
            "OccurrenceGroupV1", source_path, declaration, syntax_class,
            classification, *ids,
        ])
        if sha(serial.encode()) != digest:
            raise ValueError(f"group annex row {number}: groupDigest mismatch")
        for ident in ids:
            if ident in entries:
                raise ValueError(f"group annex row {number}: duplicate {ident}")
            entries[ident] = FrozenEntry(
                ident, source_path, declaration, syntax_class, classification, digest
            )
    harmless_count = sum(
        row.classification.startswith("harmless:") for row in entries.values()
    )
    if (len(entries), len(entries) - harmless_count, harmless_count) != (954, 431, 523):
        raise ValueError(("entry classification partition", len(entries), harmless_count))

    n_text = annex_hashes["n"][0]
    n_coverage: dict[str, tuple[str, frozenset[str]]] = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(n_text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 4:
            raise ValueError(f"N annex row {number}: expected 4 TSV fields")
        tag, disposition, count_text, ids_text = fields
        if not re.fullmatch(r"N\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+\]", tag):
            raise ValueError(f"N annex row {number}: invalid tag")
        if disposition not in ("typed", "capture", "approved-residual"):
            raise ValueError(f"N annex row {number}: invalid disposition")
        ids = (
            frozenset()
            if ids_text == "NONE"
            else frozenset(filter(None, ids_text.split(",")))
        )
        if int(count_text) != len(ids) or tag in n_coverage:
            raise ValueError(f"N annex row {number}: count/duplicate mismatch")
        n_coverage[tag] = (disposition, ids)
    disposition_counts = Counter(value[0] for value in n_coverage.values())
    if len(n_coverage) != 130 or disposition_counts != Counter({
        "typed": 89, "capture": 14, "approved-residual": 27,
    }):
        raise ValueError(("N coverage checksum", len(n_coverage), disposition_counts))
    actual_n: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for ident, row in entries.items():
        for tag, disposition in re.findall(
            r"descriptor:(N\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+\]):(typed|capture|approved-residual)",
            row.classification,
        ):
            frozen = n_coverage.get(tag)
            if frozen is None or frozen[0] != disposition:
                raise ValueError(("N disposition join", ident, tag, disposition))
            actual_n[tag].add(ident)
    for tag, (_, expected_ids) in n_coverage.items():
        if frozenset(actual_n.get(tag, set())) != expected_ids:
            raise ValueError(("N occurrence closure", tag))

    cross_text = annex_hashes["cross"][0]
    cross: set[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] = set()
    for number, line in enumerate(cross_text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 5:
            raise ValueError(f"cross annex row {number}: expected 5 TSV fields")
        row = tuple(fields)
        if row in cross:
            raise ValueError(f"cross annex row {number}: duplicate tuple")
        cross.add(row)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    if len(cross) != 248 or Counter(row[3] for row in cross) != Counter({
        "literal": 108, "catch": 140,
    }):
        raise ValueError(("cross annex checksum", len(cross)))

    gate_text = annex_hashes["gate"][0]
    gate_tags: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
    for number, line in enumerate(gate_text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 2 or fields[0] not in ("literal", "catch", "raw"):
            raise ValueError(f"gate annex row {number}: malformed gate/tag")
        row = (fields[0], fields[1])
        if row in gate_tags:
            raise ValueError(f"gate annex row {number}: duplicate gate/tag")
        gate_tags.add(row)
    if Counter(gate for gate, _ in gate_tags) != Counter({"literal": 133, "catch": 134}):
        raise ValueError(("gate/tag checksum", Counter(gate for gate, _ in gate_tags)))

    actual_cross: set[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] = set()
    for ident, row in entries.items():
        for gate, tag in re.findall(
            rf"cross:(literal|catch|raw):({SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})", row.classification
        ):
            if (gate, tag) not in gate_tags:
                raise ValueError(("unknown cross gate/tag", ident, gate, tag))
            actual_cross.add((ident, row.path, row.declaration, gate, tag))
    if actual_cross != cross:
        raise ValueError(("cross occurrence closure", len(actual_cross), len(cross)))

    exclusion_text = annex_hashes["exclusions"][0]
    exclusions: dict[str, FrozenExclusion] = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(exclusion_text.splitlines(), 1):
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) != 9:
            raise ValueError(f"exclusion annex row {number}: expected 9 TSV fields")
        ident, source_path, declaration, exclusion_class, node_kind, node, left, right, ordinal_text = fields
        if ident in exclusions or not re.fullmatch(r"(?:SX-E|SC-X)-[0-9a-f]{64}", ident):
            raise ValueError(f"exclusion annex row {number}: invalid/duplicate ID")
        ordinal = int(ordinal_text)
        if ident.startswith("SX-E-"):
            serial = "\0".join([
                source_path, declaration, exclusion_class, node, left, right,
                str(ordinal),
            ])
        else:
            if exclusion_class != "unreviewedStandaloneCallSyntax" or node_kind not in (
                "standaloneCall", "explicitDiscard",
            ):
                raise ValueError(f"exclusion annex row {number}: invalid standalone class")
            serial = "\0".join([
                source_path, declaration, node_kind, node, left, right,
                str(ordinal),
            ])
        if ident.split("-", 2)[2] != sha(serial.encode()):
            raise ValueError(f"exclusion annex row {number}: identity digest mismatch")
        exclusions[ident] = FrozenExclusion(
            ident, source_path, declaration, exclusion_class, node_kind,
            node, left, right, ordinal,
        )
    ids = sorted(exclusions)
    if (
        len(exclusions) != 2962
        or sum(ident.startswith("SX-E-") for ident in ids) != 759
        or sum(ident.startswith("SC-X-") for ident in ids) != 2203
    ):
        raise ValueError(("expanded exclusion partition", len(exclusions)))
    union_digest = sha("\0".join(["P1BExpandedSyntaxExclusionUnionV1", *ids]).encode())
    if union_digest != "808dd09fc37cf71ce6fa83a872741caf40ae6c2b4ccb904f56d3630e992758dc":
        raise ValueError(("expanded exclusion union digest", union_digest))

    return FrozenInventory(
        entries=entries,
        exclusions=exclusions,
        n_coverage=n_coverage,
        cross_coverage=frozenset(cross),
        gate_tags=frozenset(gate_tags),
        primary_seams=primary_seams,
        catch_dispositions=catch_dispositions,
        delegate_registry=delegate_registry,
    )


def load_frozen_inventory(path: Path) -> FrozenInventory:
    return load_frozen_inventory_document(path.read_text())


def load_embedded_scanner(document_path: Path) -> str:
    document = document_path.read_text()
    payload = _fenced_annex(
        document, "#### §9.1g Inline normative reference scanner source"
    )
    first, separator, remainder = payload.partition("\n")
    match = re.fullmatch(
        r"# meta\tbytes=([0-9]+)\tlines=([0-9]+)\tsha256=([0-9a-f]{64})",
        first,
    )
    if not separator or match is None:
        raise ValueError("§9.1g scanner framing drift")
    raw = remainder.encode()
    if (
        len(raw) != int(match.group(1))
        or len(remainder.splitlines()) != int(match.group(2))
        or sha(raw) != match.group(3)
        or not remainder.endswith("\n")
    ):
        raise ValueError("§9.1g scanner hash/byte/line drift")
    compile(remainder, "<embedded-§9.1g>", "exec")
    return remainder


def load_embedded_typed_registry(
    document_path: Path,
    frozen: FrozenInventory,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], list[dict[str, str]]]:
    document = document_path.read_text()
    payload = _fenced_annex(
        document, "#### §9.1h Inline compiler-typed role registry"
    )
    validator = globals().get("validate_frozen_typed_registry")
    if validator is None:
        raise ValueError("typed registry validator unavailable")
    return validator(frozen, payload)  # type: ignore[no-any-return]


def verify_entry_mode(frozen: FrozenInventory) -> dict[str, object]:
    if (
        len(ENTRY_PATHS) != 35
        or len(set(ENTRY_PATHS)) != 35
        or set(ENTRY_PATHS) != set(ENTRY_SHA256)
        or len(PLANNED_PATHS) != 8
        or len(set(PLANNED_PATHS)) != 8
        or set(ENTRY_PATHS).intersection(PLANNED_PATHS)
        or len(FINAL_PATHS) != 43
        or exact_path_vector_digest(ENTRY_PATHS) != ENTRY_PATH_VECTOR_SHA256
        or exact_path_vector_digest(FINAL_PATHS) != FINAL_PATH_VECTOR_SHA256
    ):
        raise AssertionError("closed 35 + 8 path universe/path vector is invalid")
    for path in ENTRY_PATHS:
        actual = sha((ROOT / path).read_bytes())
        if actual != ENTRY_SHA256[path]:
            raise AssertionError(("entry SHA mismatch", path, ENTRY_SHA256[path], actual))
    present_planned = [path for path in PLANNED_PATHS if (ROOT / path).exists()]
    if present_planned:
        raise AssertionError(("planned path is not literal ABSENT", present_planned))

    occurrences = [occurrence for path in ENTRY_PATHS for occurrence in collect(path)]
    occurrence_by_id = {"EF-E-" + occurrence.digest: occurrence for occurrence in occurrences}
    if len(occurrences) != 954 or len(occurrence_by_id) != 954:
        raise AssertionError(("entry occurrence count/collision", len(occurrences), len(occurrence_by_id)))
    if set(occurrence_by_id) != set(frozen.entries):
        raise AssertionError((
            "entry occurrence set mismatch",
            sorted(set(occurrence_by_id) - set(frozen.entries))[:5],
            sorted(set(frozen.entries) - set(occurrence_by_id))[:5],
        ))
    for ident, occurrence in occurrence_by_id.items():
        row = frozen.entries[ident]
        if (occurrence.path, occurrence.declaration, occurrence.syntax_class) != (
            row.path, row.declaration, row.syntax_class,
        ):
            raise AssertionError(("entry tuple mismatch", ident))
    class_counts = Counter(occurrence.syntax_class for occurrence in occurrences)
    expected_classes = Counter({
        "nilCoalescing": 200,
        "ternaryOrSwitchDefault": 171,
        "guardEarlyExit": 267,
        "dropProjection": 51,
        "optionalOrResultProjection": 23,
        "ignoredNonVoidResult": 80,
        "nonthrowingSwallowCatch": 134,
        "forceTry": 2,
        "explicitTrapCall": 9,
        "businessNumericFallback": 17,
    })
    if class_counts != expected_classes:
        raise AssertionError(("entry class vector", class_counts, expected_classes))

    core_records = [record for path in ENTRY_PATHS for record in exclusion_records(path)]
    core_ids = {"SX-E-" + record.digest for record in core_records}
    if len(core_records) != 759 or core_ids != frozen.core_exclusion_ids:
        raise AssertionError(("entry core exclusion closure", len(core_records), len(core_ids)))
    if Counter(record.kind for record in core_records) != Counter({
        "frozenLoneQuestion": 486,
        "frozenOptionalChainingDot": 159,
        "collectionMapOrFlatMap": 54,
        "queryFilter": 60,
    }):
        raise AssertionError("entry core exclusion class vector")

    call_roots = [row for path in ENTRY_PATHS for row in call_root_rows(path)]
    reviewed = [
        occurrence for occurrence in occurrences
        if occurrence.syntax_class == "ignoredNonVoidResult"
    ]
    join_entry_reviewed_roots(call_roots, reviewed)
    finalize_call_roots(call_roots)
    reviewed_rows = [row for row in call_roots if row.reviewed_id]
    exclusion_rows = [row for row in call_roots if not row.reviewed_id]
    standalone_ids = {"SC-X-" + row.digest for row in exclusion_rows}
    if (
        len(call_roots) != 2283
        or len(reviewed_rows) != 80
        or len(exclusion_rows) != 2203
        or len(standalone_ids) != 2203
        or standalone_ids != frozen.standalone_exclusion_ids
        or {row.reviewed_id for row in reviewed_rows} != {
            "EF-E-" + occurrence.digest for occurrence in reviewed
        }
        or sum(row.statement_kind == "explicitDiscard" for row in reviewed_rows) != 17
        or sum(row.statement_kind == "standaloneCall" for row in reviewed_rows) != 63
    ):
        raise AssertionError((
            "entry standalone root closure", len(call_roots), len(reviewed_rows),
            len(exclusion_rows), len(standalone_ids),
        ))

    union_ids = sorted(core_ids | standalone_ids)
    union_digest = sha("\0".join(["P1BExpandedSyntaxExclusionUnionV1", *union_ids]).encode())
    if len(union_ids) != 2962 or union_digest != (
        "808dd09fc37cf71ce6fa83a872741caf40ae6c2b4ccb904f56d3630e992758dc"
    ):
        raise AssertionError(("entry expanded exclusion closure", len(union_ids), union_digest))
    return {
        "paths": 43,
        "entryPaths": 35,
        "plannedAbsent": 8,
        "candidates": 954,
        "business": 431,
        "harmless": 523,
        "exclusions": 2962,
        "callRoots": 2283,
        "classVector": dict(sorted(class_counts.items())),
        "exclusionDigest": union_digest,
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Final-source scanner. It consumes only frozen inline truth plus final bytes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

RESOLVE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^ P1-B-RESOLVE (?:(?:KEEP (?P<keep_entry>EF-E-[0-9a-f]{64}) "
    r"(?P<keep_final>EF-F-[0-9a-f]{64}))|"
    r"(?:DELETE (?P<delete_entry>EF-E-[0-9a-f]{64}) NONE)|"
    r"(?:PLANNED (?P<planned>PF-P-[0-9a-f]{64}) "
    r"(?P<planned_final>EF-F-[0-9a-f]{64})))$"
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Resolution:
    relation_id: str
    action: str
    final_id: str
    marker_path: str
    marker_offset: int


EQUIVALENT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^ P1-B-EQUIVALENT (typed|capture|approved-residual) "
    r"(N\[\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+\])$"
)
EQUIVALENT_CROSS_RE = re.compile(
    rf"^ P1-B-EQUIVALENT-CROSS (literal|catch|raw) ({SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})$"
)
CATCH_MARKER_RE = re.compile(
    rf"^ P1-B-CATCH (typed|capture|approved-residual) ({SEMANTIC_TAG_PATTERN})$"
)
DELEGATE_RE = re.compile(r"^ P1-B-DELEGATE (DE-[0-9]{3}) ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$")
SEAM_RE = re.compile(r"^ P1-B-SEAM ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MarkerLine:
    path: str
    line_index: int
    start: int
    end: int
    body: str


@dataclass
class MarkerBlock:
    path: str
    lines: list[MarkerLine]
    code_start: int
    code_end: int
    declaration: str
    catch_occurrence: Occurrence | None = None
    declaration_block: bool = False

    @property
    def resolutions(self) -> list[Resolution]:
        parsed: list[Resolution] = []
        for line in self.lines:
            match = RESOLVE_RE.fullmatch(line.body)
            if match is None:
                continue
            if match.group("keep_entry"):
                parsed.append(Resolution(
                    match.group("keep_entry"), "KEEP", match.group("keep_final"),
                    self.path, line.start,
                ))
            elif match.group("delete_entry"):
                parsed.append(Resolution(
                    match.group("delete_entry"), "DELETE", "NONE",
                    self.path, line.start,
                ))
            else:
                parsed.append(Resolution(
                    match.group("planned"), "PLANNED", match.group("planned_final"),
                    self.path, line.start,
                ))
        return parsed


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RetainedMapSite:
    exclusion: FrozenExclusion
    start: int
    end: int


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compiler-typed role registry.  This is intentionally independent from the
# entry V1 loader below: terminal final freezes the complete entry semantic
# signature and compares it with retained V2 AST bytes only;
# it never treats successful type-checking or a name-only match as evidence.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TYPED_ROLE_SCHEMA = "P1BTypedRoleRegistryV2"
SWIFT_DRIVER_VERSION = (
    "swift-driver version: 1.127.14.1 Apple Swift version 6.2.3 "
    "(swiftlang-6.2.3.3.21 clang-1700.6.3.2)\n"
    "Target: arm64-apple-macosx26.0"
)
AST_COMPILER_VERSION = {
    "_kind": "compiler_version",
    "major": "6",
    "minor": "2",
    "full": "Apple Swift version 6.2.3 "
            "(swiftlang-6.2.3.3.21 clang-1700.6.3.2)",
}
TYPED_CONFIGS = ("debug", "release")
MAP_DECL_USRS = frozenset({
    "s:SlsE3mapySayqd__Gqd__7ElementQzqd_0_YKXEqd_0_YKs5ErrorRd_0_r0_lF",
    "s:STsE3mapySayqd__Gqd__7ElementQzqd_0_YKXEqd_0_YKs5ErrorRd_0_r0_lF",
})
MAP_RECEIVER_PROTOCOL_USRS = frozenset({"s:Sl", "s:ST"})
GRDB_FILTER_USRS = frozenset({
    "s:4GRDB11TableRecordPAAE6filteryAA21QueryInterfaceRequestVyxGqd__AA22SQLSpecificExpressibleRd__lFZ",
    "s:4GRDB11TableRecordPAAE6filter4keysAA21QueryInterfaceRequestVyxGqd___tSlRd__AA24DatabaseValueConvertibleRd_0_7ElementQyd__Rsd_0_r0_lFZ",
})
GRDB_QUERY_TERMINALS = frozenset({
    "fetchOne", "fetchAll", "fetchCursor", "fetchCount",
    "deleteAll", "updateAll",
})
TASK_CONSTRUCTOR_USR = (
    "s:ScT12_Concurrencys5NeverORs_rlE4name8priority9operation"
    "ScTyxACGSSSg_ScPSgxyYaYAcntcfc"
)
NOTIFICATION_ADD_OBSERVER_USR = (
    "c:objc(cs)NSNotificationCenter(im)addObserverForName:object:queue:usingBlock:"
)
CALL_SHAPED_CROSS_CLASSES = frozenset({"forceTry", "explicitTrapCall"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TypedLexicalSite:
    identity: str
    path: str
    declaration: str
    exclusion_class: str
    node_kind: str
    node: str
    start: int
    end: int
    candidate_links: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    # The compiler producer freezes which declaration owns an optional dot:
    # the selected member after ``?.`` or the immediately consumed inner call.
    # This is a structural selector, not a semantic authorization; the full
    # selected type/USR/module still has to compare exactly.
    optional_selection_role: str = ""


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def _byte_prefix(text: str) -> list[int]:
    result = [0] * (len(text) + 1)
    total = 0
    for index, character in enumerate(text):
        total += len(character.encode("utf-8"))
        result[index + 1] = total
    return result


def _entry_typed_sites(frozen: FrozenInventory) -> dict[str, TypedLexicalSite]:
    occurrences_by_path = {
        path: collect(path) for path in ENTRY_PATHS
    }
    sites: dict[str, TypedLexicalSite] = {}
    roots = [row for path in ENTRY_PATHS for row in call_root_rows(path)]
    reviewed = [
        occurrence
        for values in occurrences_by_path.values()
        for occurrence in values
        if occurrence.syntax_class == "ignoredNonVoidResult"
    ]
    join_entry_reviewed_roots(roots, reviewed)
    finalize_call_roots(roots)
    for row in roots:
        if row.reviewed_id:
            continue
        identity = "SC-X-" + row.digest
        # Cross-class consumption is exact-root only: the EF trigger must begin
        # at the same canonical lexical root, not merely occur somewhere in a
        # Task/View/closure statement's large source range.
        links = tuple(sorted(
            "EF-E-" + occurrence.digest
            for occurrence in occurrences_by_path[row.path]
            if occurrence.syntax_class in CALL_SHAPED_CROSS_CLASSES
            and occurrence.start == row.significant
        ))
        if len(links) > 1:
            raise ValueError((identity, "multiple exact-root candidate links", links))
        sites[identity] = TypedLexicalSite(
            identity, row.path, row.declaration,
            "unreviewedStandaloneCallSyntax", row.statement_kind,
            row.node, row.significant, row.end, links,
        )
    for path in ENTRY_PATHS:
        for row in exclusion_records(path):
            if row.kind not in {
                "collectionMapOrFlatMap", "queryFilter",
                "frozenOptionalChainingDot",
            }:
                continue
            identity = "SX-E-" + row.digest
            sites[identity] = TypedLexicalSite(
                identity, row.path, row.declaration, row.kind, row.kind,
                row.node, row.start, row.start + len(row.node), (),
            )
    expected = (
        frozen.standalone_exclusion_ids
        | {
            identity for identity, row in frozen.exclusions.items()
            if row.exclusion_class in {
                "collectionMapOrFlatMap", "queryFilter",
                "frozenOptionalChainingDot",
            }
        }
    )
    if set(sites) != expected or len(sites) != 2476:
        raise ValueError((
            "entry typed-site closure", len(sites), len(expected),
            sorted(set(sites) - expected)[:5],
            sorted(expected - set(sites))[:5],
        ))
    reverse_links = Counter(
        link for site in sites.values() for link in site.candidate_links
    )
    if any(count != 1 for count in reverse_links.values()):
        raise ValueError(("cross-class candidate is not one-to-one", reverse_links))
    return sites


def _target_for_path(path: str) -> str:
    if path.startswith("Sources/AgentLoopCore/"):
        return "AgentLoopCore"
    if path.startswith("Sources/AgentLoopApp/"):
        return "AgentLoopApp"
    if path.startswith("Sources/AgentLoopApplication/"):
        return "AgentLoopApplication"
    raise ValueError((path, "AST target unavailable"))


def _semantic_json(value: object) -> str:
    return json.dumps(
        value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False,
    )


def _validate_entry_ast_corpus_v1(
    corpus: Path,
    expected_paths: list[str],
) -> dict[tuple[str, str], Path]:
    if expected_paths != ENTRY_PATHS:
        raise ValueError("legacy V1 AST corpus is entry-only")
    manifest_path = corpus.parent / "corpus-manifest.json"
    progress_path = corpus.parent / "corpus-progress.tsv"
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
    if manifest.get("compiler_version") != SWIFT_DRIVER_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(("AST compiler version drift", manifest.get("compiler_version")))
    configs = manifest.get("configs")
    jobs = manifest.get("jobs")
    if not isinstance(configs, list) or not isinstance(jobs, list):
        raise ValueError("AST corpus manifest schema")
    config_pairs = {(row.get("config"), row.get("target")) for row in configs}
    expected_pairs = {
        (config, _target_for_path(path))
        for config in TYPED_CONFIGS for path in expected_paths
    }
    if config_pairs != expected_pairs:
        raise ValueError(("AST corpus configuration closure", config_pairs, expected_pairs))
    for row in configs:
        if set(row) != {
            "base_command", "base_dryrun_sha256", "config", "description",
            "dryrun_job_count", "record", "removed", "rewritten",
            "selected_count", "source_count", "target",
        }:
            raise ValueError(("AST config fields", sorted(row)))
        command = row["base_command"]
        if not isinstance(command, list) or command[:5] != [
            "/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/swiftc",
            "-typecheck", "-dump-ast", "-dump-ast-format", "json",
        ]:
            raise ValueError(("AST base command prefix", row["config"], row["target"]))
        joined = "\0".join(command)
        if str(ROOT) + "/.build/" in "\0".join(
            value for index, value in enumerate(command)
            if index and command[index - 1] in {"-module-cache-path", "-index-store-path"}
        ):
            raise ValueError(("AST cache routed into workspace", row["config"], row["target"]))
        if "-dump-ast-format\0json" not in joined:
            raise ValueError("AST JSON format missing")

    progress: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, str]] = {}
    progress_text = progress_path.read_text()
    if progress_text.startswith("# "):
        progress_text = progress_text[2:]
    for row in csv.DictReader(progress_text.splitlines(), delimiter="\t"):
        key = (row["config"], row["exactPath"])
        if key in progress:
            raise ValueError(("duplicate AST progress row", key))
        progress[key] = row
    expected_keys = {
        (config, path) for config in TYPED_CONFIGS for path in expected_paths
    }
    if set(progress) != expected_keys:
        raise ValueError(("AST progress closure", len(progress), len(expected_keys)))

    job_by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, object]] = {}
    for job in jobs:
        if set(job) != {"command", "config", "exactPath", "exit", "stderr", "stdout", "target"}:
            raise ValueError(("AST job fields", sorted(job)))
        key = (job["config"], job["exactPath"])
        if key in job_by_key:
            raise ValueError(("duplicate AST job", key))
        if key not in expected_keys or job["target"] != _target_for_path(job["exactPath"]):
            raise ValueError(("AST job path/target", key, job["target"]))
        command = job["command"]
        primary = str(ROOT / job["exactPath"])
        if command[:3] != [
            "/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/swiftc", "-frontend", "-dump-ast",
        ] or command.count("-primary-file") != 1:
            raise ValueError(("AST primary command prefix", key))
        primary_index = command.index("-primary-file")
        if command[primary_index + 1] != primary:
            raise ValueError(("AST primary mismatch", key))
        if command.count("-dump-ast-format") != 1 or command[command.index("-dump-ast-format") + 1] != "json":
            raise ValueError(("AST primary JSON format", key))
        if command[-2:] != ["-o", "-"]:
            raise ValueError(("AST stdout routing", key, command[-2:]))
        for forbidden in ("-emit-module", "-emit-object", "-index-store-path", "-serialize-diagnostics"):
            if forbidden in command:
                raise ValueError(("AST mutating output flag", key, forbidden))
        job_by_key[key] = job
    if set(job_by_key) != expected_keys:
        raise ValueError(("AST job closure", len(job_by_key), len(expected_keys)))

    # Return artifact paths, not materialized JSON dictionaries.  A complete
    # entry-path debug/release corpus is hundreds of megabytes on disk and several
    # gigabytes as Python objects; retaining every dump would make replay depend
    # on machine memory rather than the frozen evidence.  Validation is strictly
    # streaming, and extraction below loads at most one primary-file dump at a
    # time.
    artifacts: dict[tuple[str, str], Path] = {}
    for key in sorted(expected_keys):
        config, path = key
        target = _target_for_path(path)
        stem = path.replace("/", "__")
        ast_path = corpus / config / target / (stem + ".ast.json")
        stderr_path = corpus / config / target / (stem + ".stderr")
        exit_path = corpus / config / target / (stem + ".exit")
        progress_row = progress[key]
        if (
            exit_path.read_text().strip() != "0"
            or stderr_path.read_bytes() != b""
            or progress_row["exit"] != "0"
            or progress_row["validJSON"] != "yes"
            or progress_row["jsonKind"] != "dict"
            or progress_row["stderrBytes"] != "0"
            or progress_row["stdoutSHA256"] != sha(ast_path.read_bytes())
            or progress_row["stderrSHA256"] != sha(b"")
        ):
            raise ValueError(("AST job artifact failure", key, progress_row))
        # The producer already froze validJSON=dict plus the exact stdout
        # digest in corpus-progress.  Reading the whole AST once more merely to
        # inspect three root fields would double peak memory for large SwiftUI
        # primaries.  A bounded prefix carries all three fields in the compiler
        # JSON schema; full JSON is parsed exactly once later when that primary
        # is semantically indexed.
        with ast_path.open("rb") as handle:
            prefix = handle.read(4096).decode("utf-8")
        if (
            '"_kind":"source_file"' not in prefix
            or json.dumps(str(ROOT / path), separators=(",", ":")) not in prefix
            or all(
                json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":")) not in prefix
                for value in (AST_COMPILER_VERSION,)
            )
        ):
            raise ValueError(("AST root/schema drift", key))
        artifacts[key] = ast_path
    return artifacts


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _IndexedASTNode:
    value: dict[str, object]
    ancestors: tuple[tuple[dict[str, object], str], ...]
    # Dictionary key by which this node is attached to its immediate parent.
    # Ancestor tuples record each ancestor's own incoming edge, so without this
    # field a direct guard/if condition loses the decisive `conditions` edge.
    incoming_edge: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _ASTLookup:
    nodes: tuple[_IndexedASTNode, ...]
    expressions_by_start: dict[int, tuple[_IndexedASTNode, ...]]
    declrefs_by_start: dict[int, tuple[_IndexedASTNode, ...]]
    optional_evaluations: tuple[_IndexedASTNode, ...]


def _index_ast(dump: dict[str, object]) -> list[_IndexedASTNode]:
    result: list[_IndexedASTNode] = []
    retained_kinds = {
        "call_expr", "try_expr", "optional_try_expr", "force_try_expr",
        "await_expr", "optional_evaluation_expr", "force_value_expr",
        "assign_expr", "tuple_expr", "declref_expr", "accessor_decl",
    }
    ancestor_kinds = {
        "return_stmt", "pattern_entry", "yield_expr", "brace_stmt",
        "closure_expr", "func_decl", "accessor_decl", "constructor_decl",
        "subscript_decl", "guard_stmt", "if_stmt", "while_stmt",
        "repeat_while_stmt", "for_each_stmt", "switch_stmt", "throw_stmt",
        "rebind_self_in_constructor_expr",
    }

    def walk(
        value: object,
        ancestors: tuple[tuple[dict[str, object], str], ...] = (),
        edge: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            base_ancestors = (
                ancestors + (({"_kind": "_condition_container"}, edge),)
                if edge in {"conditions", "condition", "cond_expr"}
                else ancestors
            )
            if isinstance(value.get("_kind"), str):
                if value.get("_kind") in retained_kinds:
                    result.append(_IndexedASTNode(value, base_ancestors, edge))
                kind = str(value.get("_kind"))
                next_ancestors = (
                    base_ancestors + ((value, edge),)
                    if kind in ancestor_kinds or kind.endswith("_expr")
                    else base_ancestors
                )
            else:
                # Swift's JSON AST represents each control-flow condition as
                # an untyped dictionary below the statement's ``conditions``
                # array.  If only typed nodes are retained, a selected call's
                # immediate edge becomes ``initializer`` and the decisive
                # conditions edge disappears.  Preserve that container as a
                # tiny sentinel ancestor so a guard/if/while body can never be
                # mistaken for its compiler-consumed condition.
                next_ancestors = base_ancestors
            for key, child in value.items():
                walk(child, next_ancestors, key)
        elif isinstance(value, list):
            for child in value:
                walk(child, ancestors, edge)

    walk(dump)
    return result


def _ast_lookup(dump: dict[str, object]) -> _ASTLookup:
    nodes = _index_ast(dump)
    expression_kinds = {
        "call_expr", "try_expr", "optional_try_expr", "force_try_expr",
        "await_expr", "optional_evaluation_expr", "force_value_expr",
        "assign_expr", "tuple_expr",
    }
    expressions: dict[int, list[_IndexedASTNode]] = defaultdict(list)
    declrefs: dict[int, list[_IndexedASTNode]] = defaultdict(list)
    optionals: list[_IndexedASTNode] = []
    for item in nodes:
        value = item.value
        span = value.get("range")
        if not isinstance(span, dict) or span.get("buffer_id"):
            continue
        start = span.get("start")
        if not isinstance(start, int):
            continue
        kind = value.get("_kind")
        if kind in expression_kinds:
            expressions[start].append(item)
        if kind == "declref_expr":
            declrefs[start].append(item)
        if kind == "optional_evaluation_expr":
            optionals.append(item)
    return _ASTLookup(
        tuple(nodes),
        {key: tuple(values) for key, values in expressions.items()},
        {key: tuple(values) for key, values in declrefs.items()},
        tuple(optionals),
    )


def _decl_refs(value: object) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    result: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    def walk(item: object) -> None:
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            if item.get("_kind") == "decl_ref":
                result.append(item)
            for child in item.values():
                walk(child)
        elif isinstance(item, list):
            for child in item:
                walk(child)

    walk(value)
    return result


def _module_for_usr(usr: str) -> str:
    if usr.startswith("s:7SwiftUI"):
        return "SwiftUI"
    if usr.startswith("s:4GRDB"):
        return "GRDB"
    if usr.startswith(("s:10Foundation", "s:So", "c:objc")):
        return "FoundationOrObjC"
    if usr.startswith("s:12AgentLoopApp"):
        return "AgentLoopApp"
    if usr.startswith("s:13AgentLoopCore"):
        return "AgentLoopCore"
    if usr.startswith(("s:S", "s:s", "s:Sc")):
        return "Swift"
    return "other" if usr else ""


def _unique_indexed(values: list[_IndexedASTNode]) -> list[_IndexedASTNode]:
    unique: dict[str, _IndexedASTNode] = {}
    for item in values:
        value = item.value
        decls = _decl_refs(value.get("fn", {}))
        selected = [
            (
                str(row.get("base_name", "")), str(row.get("decl_usr", "")),
                str(row.get("type_usr", "")),
            )
            for row in decls if row.get("decl_usr")
        ]
        signature = _semantic_json({
            "kind": value.get("_kind", ""),
            "range": value.get("range", {}),
            "type": value.get("type", ""),
            "decls": selected,
            "implicit": bool(value.get("implicit")),
        })
        unique[signature] = item
    return list(unique.values())


def _callable_decl(value: object) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    """Follow only the callable spine, never receiver/argument subtrees."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        return None
    # Constructor delegation uses ``other_constructor_ref_expr`` rather than
    # declref/member_ref.  The callable-spine restriction is the authority;
    # every expression node carrying a nonempty declaration on that spine is
    # therefore admissible without a brittle kind allowlist.
    decl = value.get("decl")
    if isinstance(decl, dict) and (
        decl.get("decl_usr") or decl.get("type_usr") or decl.get("base_name")
    ):
        return decl
    for key in ("fn", "sub_expr", "src", "result"):
        found = _callable_decl(value.get(key))
        if found is not None:
            return found
    return None


def _callee_for_expression(value: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object] | None:
    # A dot-syntax function subtree also contains its receiver as an implicit
    # argument.  Looking at every decl-ref would make a call such as
    # ``defaults.set`` ambiguous between ``set``, ``defaults`` and ``self``;
    # following the AST's callable spine selects only ``set``.
    found = _callable_decl(value.get("fn"))
    if found is not None:
        return found
    for key in ("sub_expr", "src", "result"):
        child = value.get(key)
        if isinstance(child, dict):
            found = _callee_for_expression(child)
            if found is not None:
                return found
    nested: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    def calls(item: object) -> None:
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            if item.get("_kind") == "call_expr":
                nested.append(item)
            for child in item.values():
                calls(child)
        elif isinstance(item, list):
            for child in item:
                calls(child)

    # Walk the root's children, not the root itself.  A call whose ``fn`` has
    # no resolvable declaration would otherwise rediscover and recurse into
    # itself forever.
    for child in value.values():
        calls(child)
    for call in nested:
        found = _callee_for_expression(call)
        if found is not None:
            return found
    return None


def _substitution_signature(decl: dict[str, object] | None) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    if decl is None:
        return [], []
    mapping = decl.get("substitutions", {})
    if not isinstance(mapping, dict):
        return [], []
    substitutions = mapping.get("substitutions", [])
    reqs = mapping.get("reqs", [])
    replacement_types = [
        str(row.get("replacement_type", ""))
        for row in substitutions if isinstance(row, dict)
    ] if isinstance(substitutions, list) else []
    conformances: list[str] = []
    if isinstance(reqs, list):
        for row in reqs:
            if not isinstance(row, dict):
                continue
            conformance = row.get("conformance", {})
            if isinstance(conformance, dict) and conformance.get("protocol"):
                conformances.append(str(conformance["protocol"]))
    return replacement_types, sorted(set(conformances))


def _consumption_signature(
    selected: _IndexedASTNode,
    callee: dict[str, object] | None,
) -> tuple[str, str, list[str]]:
    ancestors = list(selected.ancestors)
    last_brace = max(
        (index for index, (node, _) in enumerate(ancestors)
         if node.get("_kind") == "brace_stmt"),
        default=-1,
    )
    local = ancestors[last_brace + 1:]
    builder_usrs: set[str] = set()
    for node, _ in local:
        for ref in _decl_refs(node.get("fn", {})):
            usr = str(ref.get("decl_usr", ""))
            if usr.startswith("s:7SwiftUI11ViewBuilderV"):
                builder_usrs.add(usr)
    owner_result = ""
    for node, _ in reversed(ancestors):
        if node.get("_kind") in {
            "func_decl", "accessor_decl", "constructor_decl",
            "subscript_decl", "closure_expr",
        }:
            owner_result = str(node.get("result") or node.get("type") or "")
            break
    if builder_usrs:
        return "consumedByExactFrozenBuilder", owner_result, sorted(builder_usrs)
    for reverse_index, (node, edge) in enumerate(reversed(local)):
        kind = node.get("_kind")
        if kind == "return_stmt":
            return (
                "consumedImplicitReturn" if node.get("implicit")
                else "consumedExplicitReturn",
                owner_result, [],
            )
        if kind == "pattern_entry":
            return "consumedInitializer", owner_result, []
        if kind == "assign_expr":
            return "consumedAssignment", owner_result, []
        if kind == "yield_stmt":
            return "consumedYield", owner_result, []
        if kind in {"guard_stmt", "if_stmt", "while_stmt"}:
            # ``edge`` describes how the statement is attached to its parent;
            # the condition edge is carried by the descendant path below it.
            index = len(local) - 1 - reverse_index
            descendant_edges = {
                child_edge for _, child_edge in local[index + 1:]
            }
            descendant_edges.add(selected.incoming_edge)
            if descendant_edges.intersection({"conditions", "condition", "cond_expr"}):
                return (
                    "consumedGuardCondition"
                    if kind == "guard_stmt"
                    else "consumedIfCondition"
                    if kind == "if_stmt"
                    else "consumedWhileCondition",
                    owner_result, [],
                )
    if callee is not None and callee.get("base_name") == "init":
        if any(node.get("_kind") == "constructor_decl" for node, _ in ancestors):
            return "consumedDelegatingInitializer", owner_result, []
    return "directExpressionRoot", owner_result, []


def _normal_expression_for_site(
    site: TypedLexicalSite,
    lookup: _ASTLookup,
    source: str,
) -> _IndexedASTNode | None:
